articles.title: GTA VI: all the news on Rockstar’s next entry in the Grand Theft Auto series
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI has had its release date delayed twice, and is currently scheduled to ship on November 19th, 2026.
articles.body: It’s been over a decade and two console generations since GTA V came out, and its sequel is still a work in progress. GTA VI has faced multiple delays, with developer Rockstar Games bumping back its predicted release date twice, eventually shifting to November 19th, 2026, a full year after its originally planned fall 2025 release window. Early official glimpses offered a look at the game’s protagonists, Jason and Lucia, who players will navigate around Vice City as outlaws on the run after a job goes south. Preorders have opened for the digital code-only game, offering the $79.99 standard edition and $99.99 Ultimate Edition on both PS5 and Xbox Series X / S. Rockstar Games has also responded to “CyberLeek” posts that showed sequences of the game, calling them heartbreaking and saying, “…this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time.” At about the same time, the leakers released yet another clip. Now a half-hour “extended look” has arrived full of gameplay slices and cutscenes that’s available for viewing on Netflix, as well as all over other social media channels in reaction videos before it hits YouTube at 9PM — here are some of our first impressions. Read on below for all of the news and updates about Grand Theft Auto VI.

articles.title: I tried a 240Hz 4K OLED gaming monitor and now I’m ruined
articles.summary: The Alienware AW2725Q is a 240Hz 4K OLED monitor that’s ruined me for my regular monitor.
articles.body: I keep accidentally ruining regular things for myself. I already can’t use a standard keyboard layout, and now I think I have to buy a really nice monitor. I’ve spent the last few months living with the Alienware AW2725Q, a 27-inch gaming monitor with a 240Hz 4K resolution QD-OLED panel. It’s one of a spate of gaming monitors that came out this year, all bearing the same Samsung Display panel, but with minor differences in features, ports, and looks. I plopped the AW2725Q on my desk in March, replacing my hulking 32-inch BenQ monitor I’ve been using since 2022. I hadn’t really considered getting a high-refresh-rate 4K OLED monitor before this year, for a couple of reasons. The main one is that they’re expensive: the AW2725Q is about the cheapest of them, at $900. The second is that I just don’t have that much time to game anymore, and my gaming rig wasn’t exactly in danger of exceeding 60fps on my existing monitor. And my 60Hz IPS monitor was, and is, working just fine. I was happy with it. I had a suspicion that if I tried a high-refresh-rate OLED I would no longer be fine with it. The lesson here is: trust your gut. [Image: [Image: At first, I was underwhelmed. Ninety percent of what I do at my desk is work, and you don’t really need a 240Hz OLED for Google Docs, Slack, and browser tabs. The OLED’s perfect black levels, infinite contrast, and bold colors did make watching YouTube videos a lot nicer, but that’s not really a big part of my job. My work laptop — an M1 MacBook Air — tops out at 60Hz output anyway, so the only real benefit I got from going to the Alienware on that machine was better pixel density, because the screen is physically smaller but has the same resolution as my old monitor. Actually, for non-gaming laptop use, the Alienware is a step backward, because it lacks a KVM switch or single-cable connection. I could just connect my MacBook to the BenQ’s USB-C port for power, data, and video all in one. With the AW2725Q, I need a USB hub or dongle to get that same convenience. Here’s the part where the reader will say, Nathan, you dingbat, surely you’re not going to judge a $900 gaming monitor by how convenient it is to use with a five-year-old Macbook, are you? No, that’d be silly. I also used it with a mostly six-year-old gaming PC. When I started using the Alienware monitor, my gaming rig was quite long in the tooth, with a mid-range Core i5 CPU circa 2018 and an Nvidia GTX 1070. To my surprise, though, the high-refresh-rate panel helped even when my PC was chugging along. It’s not so much the 240Hz, though, as it is the variable refresh rate technology, which lets the monitor match its panel refresh timing to the actual frame output of the GPU, as opposed to being stuck at 60Hz and grabbing whatever frame happens to be rendered at the time, which results in screen tearing. Up until now, I’ve dealt with screen tearing by, well, dealing with it, or by enabling V-Sync, or by not playing many games that involve rapid horizontal camera movements. I didn’t really notice its absence at first. Even when I upgraded my GPU (at long last) to a 4070 Super, it was so bottlenecked by my CPU that I didn’t see that much of a frame rate upgrade — possibly because I was playing the notoriously CPU-heavy act III of Baldur’s Gate III. I played Blue Prince when it came out in April; even that was a little CPU-bound. But then I upgraded my CPU from a Core i5-9400F to a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, which unbottlenecked my graphics card, and I started playing Cyberpunk 2077. Cyberpunk is a game that now — five years after it launched, and a couple years after it got good — still chews through as much CPU and GPU power as you can give it, and it’s a game that really benefits from a high-refresh-rate OLED. With my upgraded PC, I’m getting about 95fps at 4K resolution, high texture quality, and medium ray tracing, plus 2x DLSS frame gen and performance super resolution, and it looks buttery smooth thanks to adaptive refresh. Turning off super resolution and frame gen dropped my frame rate down to a stuttery 20. Maybe some of the textures looked nicer, but it’s not that fun playing a PowerPoint presentation. Screw that noise. Give me the super resolution and the fake frames; turns out my eyes can’t tell the difference. But they can tell the difference between the 56fps I got with just the actual raster power of the GPU and the 95fps I got with frame generation, and I like the second one better. I can’t believe I’m a fake frames guy. Of course, if I was still using my 60Hz monitor, and I’d never tried the OLED or experienced adaptive refresh rate, 56fps would have seemed great. But when I went back to my old monitor as prep for writing this article, Night City looked washed out. My old IPS monitor can’t display true black. Without an OLED display, Night City’s neon lights are duller, its seedy alleys lighter. Colors aren’t as vibrant, and in a late-game fight at the NCX spaceport, I could see the screen tearing every time V drew a bead on a new enemy or flung herself at them with a katana. Without the glossy bright colors and smooth motion, the game just didn’t grab me as much. Granted, most of what I use my monitor for is work, not gaming. When I went back to my old monitor for work, I didn’t mind the rougher cursor movement and less-smooth scrolling the way I thought I would. The only thing I really missed about the 27-inch 4K screen was its smaller physical size, which made my desk look less cluttered. My BenQ monitor has a three-computer KVM switch and a one-cable USB-C connection, which are much more useful for my day-to-day, since I’m often switching between different computers with the same peripherals and monitor. I rarely play Cyberpunk. Okay, maybe not rarely. More than I ought to, for sure. Here’s what’s good about the Alienware AW2725Q: * Great picture. Just phenomenal. * Adaptive refresh rate * The casing and stand are kinda navy blue in a fun way. * The power button light is RGB and can sync with compatible games. It glows yellow when I’m playing Cyberpunk. Same with the alien head logo thing on the back, but it’s on the back, so I can’t see it. * There’s a USB-C port and a USB-A port on the left side of the bottom bezel, perfect for USB-C headset and/or a wireless dongle. Here’s what I would like to be different: * There’s a bug where the screen doesn’t always come back on when the computer wakes up. Maybe it’s Windows, maybe it’s the monitor, but I don’t care for it. * There should be more USB ports. * I wish it had a KVM switch. The competing Asus monitor does. When I switch between my laptop and desktop, if I want to use the monitor’s onboard USB ports with both computers, I also have to move the monitor’s downstream USB cable. If you’re only using this with one computer, that’s not a problem. * Alienware Command Center manages to be annoying before you even install it, with its constant nags, and is poorly laid out once installed. It also downloads a dozen or more little Dell processes that run constantly. * The on-screen display is also awkward to navigate, but I’ve rarely used one that wasn’t. This isn’t the monitor’s fault, but Windows’s HDR support is still wretched. [Image: Would it be an Alienware without an RGB alien head logo? Please don’t look at my cable situation. A high-refresh-rate OLED gaming monitor is a luxury, obviously. You can get a high-refresh-rate monitor, or an OLED, or a 4K monitor, for a lot less than the $900 the Alienware costs (to say nothing of the $1,200 for the Asus monitor with the same panel, which does have a KVM switch). And the problem with luxury, as the saying goes, is that once you get used to it, it becomes a necessity. I don’t need a 240Hz OLED, given my frankly midtier gaming rig or the amount of time I actually spend gaming. But if I were to buy one — and I might! — I’d still go for a 240Hz OLED, and not a more affordable option like 144Hz. I keep monitors for a long time; 240Hz has plenty of overhead for my current gaming rig and should still feel acceptable for however long the OLED panel lasts. (I haven’t noticed any burn-in, and the panel shuts off every 4 hours or so to do a panel refresh, which is a pretty good cue to take a break) The sensible thing, once I send this thing back to Dell, would be to go back to my 60Hz BenQ, with its KVM switch and IPS panel. It’s a perfectly great monitor for the vast majority of the things I actually use a monitor for. And the OLED monitor I’d probably get — one with a KVM switch — is twelve hundred dollars. But I already saved $3,600 not getting the best keyboard on earth, so surely I’m good to spend a mere third of that on a really nice monitor, right? Photography by Nathan Edwards / The Verge

articles.title: Scott Pilgrim creator Bryan Lee O’Malley on taking ‘another run’ with new game
articles.summary: With the launch of Scott Pilgrim EX on the Switch, PS5, Xbox, and Steam, series creator Bryan Lee O’Malley talks about the game.
articles.body: It’s been a busy few years for Scott Pilgrim. Following a live-action film and the conclusion of the comics in 2010, the series has slowly been coming back to life. First, in 2021 Scott Pilgrim vs. The World: The Game was rereleased on modern consoles after years of being inaccessible. Two years later came an even bigger surprise: Scott Pilgrim Takes Off, a Netflix anime that remixed the story with an alternate take on Scott’s battle with seven evil exes. This was followed by a giant box set to celebrate the comic’s 20th anniversary, and now the series is back again with a game called Scott Pilgrim EX. According to Scott Pilgrim creator Bryan Lee O’Malley, there hasn’t been any grand plan for a series resurgence. Instead, each project naturally flowed from the last. “It just so happened that we did the show, and Universal was like, ‘What else do you want to do?’” he explains. Around the same time, O’Malley had been talking to the team at Tribute Games about potentially doing another game, so the choice was easy. “We’ve always wanted to take another run at it.” On the surface, Scott Pilgrim EX is similar to its predecessor. It’s a side-scrolling beat-’em-up like Streets of Rage or River City Ransom set in a pixelated Toronto. But instead of retelling the original Scott Pilgrim, which follows the titular slacker as he battles his new girlfriend Ramona’s seven evil exes, EX builds off of the story from Takes Off, which largely shifted Scott to the background to focus on the rest of the cast. “Where the show ended gave us some room to play with the exes and rearrange the cast,” O’Malley explains. The new game follows Scott and a cast of playable characters as they attempt to rescue Scott’s bandmates. This involves fighting off rival gangs — robots, demons, and vegans — and also traveling across time and space. [Media: For fans of the series, one of the more exciting parts of the anime was how it brought back together the same creative team from the live-action film: Takes Off featured the same cast, director Edgar Wright served as a producer, and O’Malley was writer and showrunner alongside BenDavid Grabinski. Metric even make an appearance. EX does something similar. The first Scott Pilgrim game was developed by Ubisoft, and much of the original team went on to found Tribute Games, which has made a name for itself with beat-’em-ups like TMNT: Shredder’s Revenge and Marvel Cosmic Invasion. EX also includes a killer new soundtrack from chiptune rock band Anamanaguchi, art from Paul Robertson, and while O’Malley was only partly involved in the original game, here he says he’s much more involved in the day-to-day production. It’s this element of collaboration that has made returning to Scott Pilgrim so rewarding, he says. “It was such a warm, life-affirming thing to do that show with all of those people,” O’Malley says of Takes Off. “It’s similar on the game. I’ve known these guys since we were way younger, and it’s 17 years later or something, and we’ve all grown up and see the world in different ways. When you’re doing comics, you’re all alone, and pretty much in your head all day. But over my career I’ve met so many people, and get to work with so many interesting people, and it’s always cool when I can revisit those relationships down the line.” [Media: While Tribute is developing the game, O’Malley has been focused primarily on the story, which is more expansive compared to its predecessor. He even drew a mini comic setting up a new character — Metal Scott — which was his first time drawing a Scott Pilgrim comic since 2010. “I take what they want to do and try to turn it into a story that makes sense for Scott Pilgrim each step of the way,” he says of his role on EX. “I feel like I’m the catcher in a sports analogy. People are just throwing stuff at me and I’m trying to figure out what works.” One of his goals with the game, and all of the more recent Scott Pilgrim projects, is to be welcoming to newcomers. The Scott Pilgrim story has now existed for two decades in various forms across comics, games, film, and television. That can make it seem intimidating from the outside. “I want everything I do to be accessible,” O’Malley explains. “Maybe it’s from growing up with comics. They’d always be telling you who the characters are, and you’d be able to catch up really quick. That’s my ethos nowadays for Scott Pilgrim. It should make sense to the faithful, but it should also be a clean entry point for anyone.” It’s unclear if or how Scott Pilgrim might continue to evolve in the future after the launch of EX. But for O’Malley, after years of getting to dabble in new formats and collaborate with old friends, he’s looking forward to returning to his roots. “I really want to get back to comics,” he says, “because I miss having all of the power. It’s been really fun to collaborate with so many talented people, but at the end of the day I miss when I just did the comic and no one really told me what to do. So hopefully I’ll get back to that soon.” Scott Pilgrim EX launches March 3rd on the Switch, Xbox, PlayStation, and PC.

articles.title: The QD-OLED gaming monitor that started it all got a big upgrade
articles.summary: If it’s ultrawide Primary RGB Tandem or Penta Tandem OLED monitors you want, Alienware will have them later in 2026.
articles.body: Alienware is taking to this year’s Computex 2026 in Taipei to announce some cool gaming monitors, most notably two exciting OLED options that are coming at different points this year. First off, the company is debuting the successor to its very first QD-OLED gaming monitor from 2022 with a refreshed design and high-end specs that’s coming in July (price hasn’t yet been shared). The AW3426DW is a 34-inch curved 3,440 x 1,440 resolution with an 1800R curve, just like its predecessor. But the new model has the latest QD-OLED Penta Tandem screen tech that boosts the peak brightness to 1,300 nits from 1,000 nit in the previous version. Its refresh rate has been boosted from 240Hz to 280Hz. [Image: [Image: Part of the five-layer Penta Tandem tech is an anti-reflective screen coating that supposedly cuts down glare and boosts deep blacks even in well-lit rooms. That’s great since black sometimes appears purple-ish on previous QD-OLED generations. Something that hasn’t changed model-to-model is pixel density; this one’s still at 110 pixels per inch, which is a bit low for this size (many 27-inch OLED monitors have a similar pixel density). Alienware’s flagship monitor of the show is a 39-inch 5K curved ultrawide monitor coming this fall that uses LG Display’s fourth-generation Primary RGB Tandem screen tech. The AW3926QW is slightly curvier than the QD-OLED model mentioned above, measuring at 1500R, making it more immersive. It can show a peak brightness of 1,300 nits while displaying content at up to 5K at a 165Hz refresh rate, with a pixel density of 143 pixels per inch. It offers a dual mode to knock the resolution down to 1080p, bumping up the refresh rate to 330Hz with support for custom resolutions and aspect ratios. [Image: [Image: The two OLED models have some traits in common with each other, despite using different screen technology. For one, both use RGB stripe subpixels to sharpen text and other details. Color-fringed text has been an issue for some people with previous generations of QD-OLED panels, but not as much with OLEDs. Both have VESA DisplayHDR True Black 500 certification, as well as Dolby Vision HDR support, and both support AMD FreeSync Premium Pro and Nvidia G-Sync. Also, they’re protected by Alienware’s great three-year warranty that covers manufacturer defects along with burn-in coverage, plus enhanced pixel shifting and refreshing algorithms to extend their lifespan. Despite the similarities, the 5K monitor simply offers more features. It has a KVM switch to let you control multiple PCs through the monitor with a single keyboard and mouse, plus a USB-C video port with support for 90W of PD passthrough power. Beyond that, it has two HDMI 2.1 ports with fixed rate link (FRL) to let PCs display its full resolution and refresh rate, one of which supports eARC and ARC. It also boasts a single DisplayPort 2.1 port with fast UHBR20 bandwidth. The 34-inch model has two HDMI 2.1 FRL ports and a DisplayPort 1.4 port. No price has been announced for the 5K display, but these features won’t come cheap. [Image: The $399.99 34-inch curved model is pictured here. Finally, Alienware has two VA LCD gaming monitors coming in July for well under $500. The $399.99 34-inch ultrawide AW3426DWM and the $299.99 flat AW3226DM have respectable specs. Both go up to 240Hz refresh rate with 1-millisecond response time and display 1440p resolution. They feature similar design language to Alienware’s higher-end options, and they support Dolby Vision HDR. It’s nice to have affordable options, though remember that Alienware’s entry-level 27-inch QD-OLED monitor is $399.99, and by nature of its screen tech, offers much better contrast and color accuracy than either of these upcoming models. It’s a stellar value for the price, as I discovered when I put my own money down on one.

articles.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore Disney+ Release Looks Likely, Fans Say
articles.summary: Marvel's newly-extended Avengers: Endgame Encore looks set for a Disney+ release after its theatrical run.
articles.body:
Marvel's newly-extended Avengers: Endgame Encore looks set for a Disney+ release after its theatrical run.

That's according to fans who have found a Disney+ listing for the upcoming re-release, which already allows fans to watch its trailer. To date, Disney has made no mention of the Endgame re-release being anything but a theatrical event, but an eventual Disney+ debut does make sense.

This week, comments from Avengers directors Joe and Anthony Russo have been widely shared online in which the duo claim that Endgame is "required viewing" for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday . Why not make its upcoming enhanced edition available to the widest possible audience, if that is indeed the case?

Yesterday, Marvel clarified that the four minutes of extra footage added to Endgame Encore would supplemented by even more for viewers who watch the film on IMAX or Disney Infinity Vision-approved screens . In other words, two versions of Endgame Encore are on their way. Which version will eventually turn up on Disney+? We'll have to wait and see.

For now, it likely makes sense for Disney to wait before announcing if and when Endgame Encore will get its streaming debut, as Marvel encourages fans to buy cinema tickets to enjoy the Infinity Saga's epic conclusion on the biggest screen possible (and to boost Endgame's box office total further).

Would you go see Endgame Encore in theaters if you knew for sure that a Disney+ launch was coming eventually? Perhaps. But others might decide that their curiosity for the movie's new scenes can wait until they can stream it.

Avengers Endgame: Encore releases in theaters on September 25, ahead of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18. Looking for more Avengers fun on Disney+ in the meantime? Ms. Marvel herself, Iman Vellani, has been roped in for a new limited video podcast series recapping the MCU's best moments — even though her character has not (yet) been confirmed to appear in Doomsday itself.

articles.title: Project Motor Racing Adding Nine New Cars, New Track Next Month
articles.summary: The V8 Power Pack, featuring historic US muscle and Gen 3 Australian V8 Supercars, arrives on September 15.
articles.body:
Giants Software and Straight4 Studios have announced the details of a new DLC pack launching for Project Motor Racing next month: the V8 Power Pack. The pack will feature nine V8 race cars from multiple eras of racing, plus a fully scanned Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta. The pack will arrive on September 15.

The V8 Power Pack will add three new classes to the garage, listed below:

“V8 Evo,” which includes the 2023 Australian-spec versions of the Ford Mustang and Chevrolet Camaro that compete in Australia’s modern Supercars racing series.

“USV8,” which adds the 2022 Dodge Challenger TA/2, the 2022 Ford Mustang TA/2, and 2022 Camaro TA/2.

“Historic USV8,” which boasts a handful of classic muscle cars in classic Trans Am road racing trim, including the 1970 Ford Mustang Boss 302, 1970 Plymouth Barracuda, 1970 AMC Javelin, and the iconic 1968 Camaro Z28.

The V8 Power Pack comes on the heels of July’s Aussie Rivals pack , which was released for free and contains an older pair of Australian V8s in the form of the 2013 Holden VF Commodore and a “completely reworked” 2013 Ford Falcon FG.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

articles.title: Of course Samsung made a 1,100Hz gaming monitor
articles.summary: Samsung announced its upcoming lineup of Odyssey gaming monitors will feature “world-first innovations” across display speeds and design.
articles.body: Samsung announced its upcoming lineup of Odyssey gaming monitors today at Gamescom, and says that several will feature “world-first innovations” across display speeds and design. This includes the 27-inch Odyssey G6 it initially unveiled in December, which now features a 1,100Hz refresh rate, alongside new OLED Odyssey G9, G8, and G7 updates for 2027. The Odyssey G6 G60H’s upgraded 1,100Hz final launch specification is a smidge faster than the already ridiculous 1,040Hz refresh rate that Samsung announced it would have at CES 2026. Little has changed otherwise, so this is still a dual-mode gaming monitor with an IPS-based display and a 1ms response time. That also means the ultra-fast refresh rate can only be achieved at 1080p, though switching to the native 1440p mode still delivers 600Hz. The real-world practicality of overkill refresh rates is hotly debated. I can’t quite fathom why Samsung would bother giving the G6 another 60Hz bump in the first place, but perhaps the company believes you’ll actually see a difference. That, or 1,100Hz just sounds braggier compared against LG’s 1,000Hz UltraGear gaming monitor that’s expected to ship in September. Samsung hasn’t specified a price or date for the Odyssey G6 launch, but says it’ll be globally available by the end of 2026. [Image: Samsung is even still using the same background display for the Odyssey G6 G60H in its marketing imagery. Samsung also introduced the new Odyssey OLED G9, and says it’s the “world’s first 49-inch DQHD gaming monitor with a 360Hz refresh rate.” While the previous model could only reach up to 240Hz, this new G9 ultra-wide has two options: 360Hz at 5120 x 1440, or an even faster 720Hz when switched to the 2560 x 720 dual HD mode. Other notable specs include a 0.03ms response time, and a peak brightness of up to 1,300 nits. [Image: [Image: Rounding off the new announcements is the 32-inch Odyssey OLED G8, which allows users to switch between UHD at 360Hz, QHD at 520Hz, and FHD at 680Hz, and the Odyssey OLED G7, which is the “world’s first 42-inch 16:9 curved OLED gaming monitor,” according to Samsung. The latter features a 4K resolution, 165Hz refresh rate, and 1000R curvature, while being larger than the previous 32-inch G7 model. [Image: [Image: Samsung hasn’t announced any prices or launch dates for the 2027 Odyssey lineup yet, but says that availability will vary by market.

articles.title: Top Gear Revival Confirmed, With Comedian Jimmy Carr Reportedly Tipped for Presenter Role
articles.summary: Top Gear has been confirmed to return, with comedian Jimmy Carr reportedly in talks for a presenter role.
articles.body:
Top Gear has been confirmed to return, with comedian Jimmy Carr reportedly in talks for a presenter role.

The BBC's globally-beloved motoring series has been off air for four years, since a major crash left former co-host Andrew "Freddie" Flintoff with serious injuries. The presenter later received a £9 million settlement in compensation for the incident.

Last week, U.K. tabloid newspaper The Sun claimed that standup star Jimmy Carr was in talks to join the series for a then-unannounced reboot. Well, he does have the perfect last name.

Today, the BBC itself has now confirmed that it is mounting plans for a Top Gear revival — though stopped short of announcing any talent attached.

"There has been a lot of speculation about this and we can confirm that Top Gear is coming back," the corporation's director of entertainment Ed Havard said, via BBC News .

"I'm not going to talk about talent today," Havard continued. "Jimmy would be a great host but I won't be discussing that today. We will have more information on Top Gear shortly."

Earlier this year, Amazon Prime's rival series The Grand Tour confirmed plans for its own return , something that may have spurred the BBC on with its own Top Gear comeback. Indeed, original Top Gear hosts Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May will appear in The Grand Tour's new season, despite handing over their full-time presenting duties.

articles.title: Strange New Worlds, After Weeks of Misfires, Finally Gets Back on Track With a Riff on 24... and The Poseidon Adventure
articles.summary: After a few missteps in recent weeks, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds gets back on the horse and rides it right into, thankfully, a slipstream wormhole for an exciting and at times emotional episode.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 6, “Off-Hour.”

Now that’s more like it. After the past several weeks of high-concept / low-impact Strange New Worlds episodes, the show finally gets back on track with a good old space adventure. Sure, it’s still a concept episode in its way (or two, I suppose, doing The Poseidon Adventure in space alongside an hour of Jack Bauer-style, real-time 24 action), but it’s one that works in spades and is never overshadowed by its concepts.

“Off-Hour” certainly benefits from its focus on two of the show’s best characters, Dr. M’Benga (Babs Olusanmokun) and Nurse Chapel (Jess Bush), and the relationship that has been established between the two over the course of the past three and a half seasons. But beyond that, the episode also gives us some nice Scotty (Martin Quinn)/Pelia (Carol Kane) interplay. And it’s also just a cracking good hour of drama, action, and sci-fi spectacle.

When the Enterprise gets stuck in a slipstream wormhole, the devastation wreaked on the ship is abrupt – and fatal for some. Then there’s the crewmembers like M’Benga, who survives the initial blast but is mortally wounded; the doctor specifically is trapped behind a medical bay table, which has crashed into him and essentially severed his body at the midsection. Once the table is moved, he’ll be dead. But that’s where Chapel comes in…

I just mentioned in my interview with Olusanmokun a couple of weeks ago that the thing about Dr. M’Benga is we know he’s going to survive the show, because his character shows up on The Original Series. But somehow that knowledge doesn’t take the tension out of his predicament this week, perhaps because Strange New Worlds plays so fast and loose with continuity that I was actually thinking while watching, “Maybe that’s a different M’Benga on The Original Series!” But also because the relationship between M’Benga and Chapel is so well-realized that just seeing them deal with this situation, and the emotion between them, is gripping in and of itself.

It’s also magnified by the fact that we learn here that M’Benga is thinking about leaving the Enterprise, and has even called in Dr. Boyce (Brian Markinson, who has previously appeared on TNG, DS9, and Voyager!) – the former (interim) chief medical officer of the Enterprise – to presumably replace him when he leaves. This is intriguing because we at home know that Strange New Worlds only has a handful of episodes left (including the abbreviated next and final season), and so characters like M’Benga and La’an who aren’t on The Original Series are going to have to start to depart the show at some point – and will be doing so one way or another, for better or worse.

Episode writer Bill Wolkoff, director Dan Liu, and the production team manage to depict space-travel danger here in a way that we have rarely seen in the franchise, as when the gravity controls onboard begin to malfunction, crushing pianos and whatnot, or when Spock and La’an have to climb onto the exterior of the ship during a pyrotechnic neutrino storm. And Scotty learning to “feel” the Enterprise and interpret its status like some kind of starship whisperer is also a nice touch, a call back (call forward?) to the Scotty who will someday say that he could tell the speed his ship was traveling “by the feel of the deck plates.”

I’m actually surprised at how much I’ve come to enjoy this version of Scotty, even as the frequent focus on him has meant that Kane’s Pelia usually takes a back seat. But here the mentor/mentee interplay between the two really works, as we see how she is helping to mold him into the man we all know he’s becoming. That all the problems the crew are facing end with a technobabble solution was perhaps inevitable, but it doesn’t make what has come before any less exciting or moving, and if anything, “Off-Hour” is a reminder that when Strange New Worlds cooks, it really cooks.

Questions and Notes from the Q Continuum:

Of course, this isn’t the first time Star Trek has done a “disaster in space” episode. Just look at TNG’s appropriately named “Disaster” for starters.

Pour one out for all those poor, irradiated bastards in Engineering who didn’t make it out after the blast doors shut. Red Shirts galore!

Dr. Phil Boyce was the original doctor on the Enterprise, first (and only, until now) seen in the unaired pilot of The Original Series, “The Cage.” There he was played by John Hoyt and depicted as a kindly and wise friend to Jeffrey Hunter’s Captain Pike – who also had a talent for making martinis. But interestingly, by the time of the second pilot, “Where No Man Has Gone Before” (where William Shatner made his debut), neither M’Benga nor Boyce was the chief medical officer onboard. Rather, Dr. Mark Piper (Paul Fix) served in that capacity for a one-episode stint before DeForest Kelley’s Dr. Leonard McCoy finally showed up. So how this will all work out remains to be seen.

Again with the gore! M’Benga being cut in half I get, and the episode is pretty restrained in how it depicts it. But then they just had to show us Una’s compound fracture and Chapel’s finger breaking off. How many fingers have we lost this season now?

articles.title: Batman: Bad Seeds - Sunset #1 Review: How DC’s Newest Gotham Crossover Pushes the Dark Knight Into a Brutal Conflict
articles.summary: DC's latest Batman crossover kicks off in Batman: Bad Seeds - Sunset #1, but should you read it? Check out our full review to find out.
articles.body:
One of the reasons I dropped out of the comic book reviewing game for so long is that I became frankly exhausted by the perpetual cycle of crossover events dominating the Big Two publishers. The Batman franchise has certainly been no stranger to those crossovers in recent years - Joker War, Knight Terrors, Gotham War - with the third storyline in particular being a frustrating mess I'd just as soon delete from my memory banks. I can't say I particularly relished the prospect of the Bat-line being overtaken by another two-month crossover, but Bad Seeds ultimately makes a decent case for itself in its opening chapter.

With Bad Seeds, DC has a couple of cards in its favor this time around. This is an event comic centered around Matt Fraction's Batman and G. Willow Wilson's Poison Ivy, two of the best ongoing books on the stands right now. It's also a story that springs pretty naturally out of the pages of the latter book. The idea being that Pamela Isley has reached the dramatic endpoint in her short tenure as mayor of Gotham City. Faced with an armed insurrection by Commissioner Vandal Savage and his officers, Ivy ushers in a contingency plan that threatens to transform the city back into a primal jungle. Naturally, the extended Bat-family has issues with that.

As mentioned, Bad Seeds is geared toward Fraction's Batman and Wilson's Poison Ivy books (though pretty much every Batman-adjacent series will be tying into the event), so it's only fitting that the two writers collaborate on this opening chapter. The duo manage to craft a largely cohesive and stylistically coherent script. By the end, we have a clear sense of the scope and stakes of this crossover. Most impressive is how efficient Bad Seeds: Sunset #1 is at establishing the massive cast of characters and their respective roles within the story. There are a lot of moving parts here, but the issue never feels overly bogged down because of it.

That being said, while Sunset #1 juggles the large ensemble cast deftly enough, it doesn't necessarily make a strong case for why readers need to branch out and follow those many tie-in books. These characters look to be playing the same part they always do in these Bat-crossovers, dealing with the general chaos unfolding across the city while Batman battles his way to the root of the conflict.

The various scenes involving Batman's friends and sidekicks are fine, but they're very much secondary to the twin core story threads involving Ivy and Batman themselves. The Ivy scenes are where much of the dramatic weight of the book stems from, as we see a woman walled in by circumstance and struggling to figure out how to outmaneuver her enemies. As for Batman, the book taps into one of the elements that has made Fraction's run such a treat - the deep compassion Bruce shows to both his enemies and the people he's sworn to protect. His run has and continues to evoke Batman: The Animated Series in that way.

Helping to maintain cohesion between Wilson and Fraction's writing is the fact that the entire issue is rendered by Giuseppe Camuncoli and Cliff Rathburn (with the former handling layouts and the latter the finished artwork). The result doesn't entirely measure up to Camuncoli's solo work, as there's a certain sinister angularity to his figures that's smoothed over by Rathburn's finishes. Still, the book is cleanly rendered and plenty dynamic, and the artists play their part in ensuring that Bad Seeds: Sunset is an approachable, entertaining gateway into a much bigger story.

articles.title: Forza Horizon 6 PS5 Launch Reportedly Scrubbed for 2026
articles.summary: Forza Horizon 6 has reportedly had its previous PlayStation 5 launch window scrubbed, with the celebrated Xbox racer no longer likely to release in 2026.
articles.body:
Forza Horizon 6 has reportedly had its previous PlayStation 5 launch window scrubbed, with the celebrated Xbox racer no longer likely to release in 2026.

That's according to The Verge senior reporter Tom Warren, who wrote on X/Twitter today that he no longer expected the port to arrive before the end of this year. IGN also understands this to be accurate.

As of yet, however, Xbox has not formally announced any change to its plans to launch Forza Horizon 6 on PS5. IGN has contacted the company for comment.

Recent months have seen a noticeable shift in emphasis by Xbox, as the company pulls back from some of its multiplatform efforts. Logos for the PS5 and Switch 2 are noticeably absent from some of Xbox's recent game trailers (after their inclusion was dubbed a "miss" by Xbox boss Asha Sharma back in May). A month later, it was reported that Xbox had pulled a trailer for Halo: Campaign Evolved from Sony's June PlayStation State of Play broadcast at the last minute. And, of course, both Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution have now been confirmed to be permanent Xbox console exclusives .

Sharma previously said that the company would honor the multiplatform launch of any title it had previously announced — such as for Forza Horizon 6, or the just-released Halo: Campaign Evolved. However, no promise was made for when these ports would actually arrive, or how they would be prioritized or promoted.

There's no suggestion that Forza Horizon 6's PS5 port has been scrapped outright, then (and indeed, the game will likely sell very well when it hits Sony's console). But a delay would certainly fit with Xbox's recent shift in focus, back to promoting its own consoles as the starting point to play its own games, and a push for the remainder of this year on October's Gears of War: E-Day.

#ForzaHorizon6 is coming to @Playstation , and the best part is that wishlists are now open! pic.twitter.com/t3OJVBBr7T — Forza Horizon (@ForzaHorizon) January 22, 2026

#ForzaHorizon6 is coming to @Playstation , and the best part is that wishlists are now open! pic.twitter.com/t3OJVBBr7T

And then, of course, there's the GTA 6 issue. After October, few games are daring fit their release around what is likely to be the best-selling game of the console generation, let alone this year. The November launch of Rockstar's long-awaited blockbuster, is heavily tied to Sony and its PS5 console through marketing deals . Even the stellar Forza Horizon 6 would likely best avoid such a hubbub.

Whenever Forza Horizon 6 does arrive on PS5, though, fans of Playground Games' racing series have a lot to look forward to. "The new standard in open-world racing is here, and it’s a gundamn masterpiece," IGN wrote in our Forza Horizon 6 review , which returned a perfect 10/10 score.

articles.body:
Microsoft is set to release a limited number of Xbox Series X - X25 Special Edition consoles in honor of the 25th anniversary of the original Xbox. This eye-catching translucent green console costs $899.99 and releases on November 13. It comes with a controller in the same retro OG Xbox style, as well as a digital copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved. Preorders have started rolling out, but they're selling out very quickly .

Here’s where you’ll be able to get it when preorders go live:

The following retailer usually sells Xbox hardware, but it doesn't have a listing yet. If/when it does, the console should appear at this link:

Microsoft is only making 25,000 of these consoles, and each one is numbered with a unique engraving. The console itself is translucent green, giving you a glimpse at the metallic insides of the machine, and labeled with “XBOX 25” on the front. It comes with a controller done up in the same translucent “OG green” style, that calls back to the original Duke controller in a number of its details.

It has a 1TB SSD and includes a digital copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved, a full remake of the original game’s campaign, plus a few brand-new levels. IGN critic Michael Higham enjoyed it pretty well, according to his review . Overall, this is a pretty great homage to the original Xbox hardware Microsoft released on November 15, 2001.

If you don’t want the console, you can preorder the X25 Special Edition Xbox Controller separately right now — but it’s selling out fast as well.

After two console generations of falling behind, Xbox has been on something of a roll lately. While PlayStation has bungled its announcement of its switch to an all-digital future , Microsoft seems to be handling the disc-to-digital transition more smoothly . It’s kickstarting a program that will let players turn their physical games into working digital copies . Of course, Microsoft has a long way to go if it wants to get back into head-to-head competition with Sony, but it may be on the right track.

And in the meantime, Microsoft can do its most dedicated fans a solid by offering an appealing new 25th anniversary console. That is, assuming stock holds out long enough for fans can get their hands on one.

articles.title: LIVE: Rockstar Finally Reveals Official GTA 6 Gameplay, First on Netflix
articles.summary: Today is the day Rockstar Games finally pulls back the curtain on the most anticipated video game of all time: Grand Theft Auto 6 — and IGN is reporting live with all the news from across the internet.
articles.body:
We visited Rockstar North to see GTA 6 and came away seriously impressed by a live gameplay demo . The 30-minute play session showcased a Grand Theft Auto with a huge emphasis on the little details that make an open world feel like a real place.

We spoke to Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, to learn about how GTA 6 is building on the series’ almost 30-year legacy: “It’s a Step Forward in All Respects.”

Across both the new “Extended Look” video and the demo session we saw at Rockstar, we’ve learned many new gameplay details .

GTA 6 will feature ‘a Very Big Map’ that’s home to its most complex world yet.

That world features the same style of satirical humour GTA is historically known for, but Rockstar admits it has to be “careful” with its jokes .

The developer considered four protagonists for GTA 6 before settling on a criminal couple.

Jason and Lucia’s Bonnie and Clyde-style romance is optional , and can be played more like a platonic partnership.

With over a decade of anticipation, Rockstar is “nervous” about the pressure to deliver .

The new wanted level system adds deeper complexity to GTA 6’s police chases.

Car jacking has been significantly upgraded , with luxury vehicles featuring advanced security systems and electronic keys that must be cloned.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

Today is the day Rockstar Games finally pulls back the curtain on the most anticipated video game of all time: Grand Theft Auto 6 — and IGN is reporting live with all the news from across the internet.

GTA 6 was confirmed four-and-a-half years ago, when Rockstar said work on the next game in the phenomenally successful franchise was in development. Following two trailers and two public delays, we are now about to get an official gameplay reveal. Netflix goes first with its Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look , which remains exclusive to the streaming platform for six hours. Netflix has said this reveal was captured entirely from in-game footage on PlayStation 5, and runs 27 minutes.

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look Netflix and YouTube global release times:

In the run up to today’s reveal, Rockstar has suffered a long list of gameplay leaks, which it responded to earlier this week . But enthusiasm for GTA 6 continues ahead of its November 19, 2026 release, and we’ll have all the news as it happens throughout the day, including the Netflix reveal itself and beyond.

So check out our live reporting below as the action unfolds. You won’t want to miss this one!

69 Images from Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look

We've got 69 images from Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look, if you want to take a closer look at Rockstar's gameplay reveal.

The GTA 6 map size compared to other Rockstar games

As reported by The New York Times , GTA 6's Vice City is twice the size of Los Santos in GTA 5. Rockstar also told the publication that the overall map is three times as large as the playable area of Red Dead Redemption 2. Yep, that's really, really big.

GTA 6 will take a while for players to finish, with the game's producer stating it took him 80 hours. In a The New York Times interview, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game back in February. He noted that timeframe included the main story and some "optional goals with narrative ramifications," so it's unclear if that included just mucking about in the open world. Still, that is a sizable length regardless. Nelson ultimately hopes fans take their time with the game and don't rush through it.

Here's Every GTA 6 Side Activity We've Spotted So Far

The GTA 6 gameplay reveal featured a number of side activities that will no doubt keep us busy for hours. Some of these look to be full mini-games, such as a clip of a rally racing track we were treated to at one point, while others, such as acquiring base-jumping equipment and leaping off a very tall building, look to be fun extras.

Most of the reaction I'm seeing online arevery positive about the visuals of GTA 6. At the end of the reveal we're told the gameplay was "captured on PS5," so we know what to expect from the game on Sony's console. I'm extremely impressed by the level of detail, the fluidity of animations, and the density of the environments, even at enormous scale. Very impressive indeed!

Here's Every Song Featured in Rockstar's GTA 6 Extended Look

Rockstar's first official extended look at GTA 6 features a lot of licensed music, and we've got the list of every song it featured right here .

The GTA 6 gameplay is now live on Netflix, and IGN has loads of fresh exclusive content on the game. We've got new screenshots, below, including one exclusive to IGN.

Only 30 minutes remain before the GTA 6 gameplay reveal on Netflix. Not long now!

Rockstar and Florida Officials Are Reportedly Talking About Turning Miami Into Vice City IRL for GTA 6 Marketing Campaign

Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for GTA 6's marketing campaign. As initially reported by The Miamian , Miami-Dade County has had formal conversations with Rockstar about a GTA 6-themed takeover of Miami to promote the upcoming game. More here .

GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Screenshots

Helldivers 2 Boss Happy That GTA 6 Is Skipping PC at Launch and There's No Online Right Away

Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried. More here .

Analysis of overnight cryptocurrency transactions points to the prolific GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out" of their meme coin, earning around $270,000 in the process. More here .

Rockstar then released GTA 6 Trailer 2 in May 2025 , a year-and-a-half after Trailer 1. Anticipation was fever pitch at this point, with fans going down increasingly elaborate rabbit holes in their bid for new details and release date. The release of Trailer 2 came hot on the heels of a delay to GTA 6 itself , from fall 2025 to May 2026 (it would go on to be delayed again, to November 19, 2026).

GTA 6 Trailer 2 was captured on base PS5, as today's reveal is. "Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them," Rockstar said in the official description released at the time. "But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive."

If you need a refresh, Trailer 2 is below:

Rockstar formally announced GTA 6 in December 2023 with the release of Trailer 1. The developer confirmed the Trailer 1 launch window a month prior, issuing a rare statement from Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser:

Next month marks the 25th anniversary of Rockstar Games.

Thanks to the incredible support of our players worldwide, we have had the opportunity to create games we are truly passionate about — without you, none of this would be possible, and we are so grateful to all of you for sharing this journey with us.

In 1998, Rockstar Games was founded on the idea that video games could come to be as essential to culture as any other form of entertainment, and we hope that we have created games you love in our efforts to be part of that evolution.

We are very excited to let you know that in early December, we will release the first trailer for the next Grand Theft Auto.

We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with all of you.

In the end, Rockstar was forced to release GTA 6 Trailer 1 early due to a leak (GTA 6 and leaks have a long history). If you're struggling to remember what was in it, check out Trailer 1 below.

Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have RPG Mechanics Like Eating, Exercising, and More

Ahead of the Netflix reveal, a cover story for Dazed magazine , revealed new information about GTA 6, which we've rounded up here . Highlights include players being able to eat, work out, and sleep, each of which has an impact on the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia.

articles.title: Peter Cullen, Optimus Prime in Transformers, Dies at 85
articles.summary: Peter Cullen, the voice of Optimus Prime in Transformers and countless other roles, has died at 85.
articles.body:
Peter Cullen, the voice of Optimus Prime in Transformers and countless other roles, has died at 85.

The legendary TV and movie voice actor passed away at his home Wednesday, August 26, his family and agent confirmed to TMZ . Additional details regarding his death have not been announced at this time.

A Canada-born actor since the '60s with decades of voice and on-camera work, Cullen has a long history of bringing his strong-and-gentle talents to movies and TV, but his most famous work is easily his role as Autobot leader and Transformers hero Optimus Prime. The character has remained one of the prevailing fictional figures of the '80s, thanks in no small part to the part Cullen played in bringing him to life.

Cullen first played Optimus Prime for the original Transformers series and returned to bring his iconic delivery to the world of Cybertron in countless sequels, spinoffs, and adaptations in the decades that followed. You may have missed him in the first Transformers movie or the War for Cybertron video game that released in 2010, for example, but there's still a good chance you caught Cullen returning to the Autobots for live-action Transformers movies like 2023's Rise of the Beasts or 2017's The Last Knight.

Cullen was an icon in the voice acting world, and there's no question that his role as Optimus Prime will stand the test of time, but his credits extend far beyond a universe of transforming alien semi-trucks. The actor also notably brought his low-register delivery to Disney classics as Winnie the Pooh's pessimistic donkey friend, Eeyore. He also chipped into the Predator universe as its first Predator and even played a role in 1976's King Kong.

Knight Rider, Spider-Man, Voltron, My Little Pony, G.I. Joe, and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles; the list goes on. TV fans most recently would have caught him as Thaedus in Invincible, but his contributions to entertainment will not be forgotten anytime soon.

"Peter Cullen passed away peacefully, surrounded by his loving family — and held in the hearts of his many friends and countless fans worldwide," his family said in a statement. "His family asks that you honor his remarkable legacy by serving your communities and leading others with compassion, integrity, and loyalty and always remember 'be strong enough to be gentle.'"

articles.title: The Witcher 3 Price Quietly Increased Ahead of Remaster Release
articles.summary: The Witcher 3 has gotten a price increase ahead of the release of the game's remaster next month.
articles.body:
The Witcher 3 has gotten a price increase ahead of the release of the game's remaster next month.

Earlier this week, CD Projekt Red surprised fans by announcing a new remaster for The Witcher 3 . It will feature visual enhancements, changes to combat, and much, much more. The best part? It's completely free to existing owners of The Witcher 3 and if you don't already own the DLCs, you're getting those for free. However, if you haven't bought the game, you will now have to pay a bit extra.

The price of The Witcher 3: Complete Edition on Steam has jumped from $39.99 to $49.99 since the announcement of the remaster. This will be the price of the remaster itself, so fans who buy the existing version are essentially paying for the new version upfront since their copy will be automatically upgraded. It's not a huge jump, but may be a bummer for those who have been waiting for the right opportunity to buy The Witcher 3 and now have to pay a bit more, especially since the game is 11 years old.

The Witcher 3 is arguably worth the price of admission, though. The game, with all of its DLCs and side quests, is hundreds of hours long and is highly replayable. It's one of the best RPGs of all-time and there's a new DLC for the game releasing next year ahead of The Witcher 4's expected release in 2028 . As noted, CD Projekt Red also offers deep discounts on The Witcher 3 constantly (I got the Complete Edition for $4 on Steam last Christmas). It wouldn't be surprising if the game goes on sale by the end of the year or in time for the game's new DLC next year, if you don't want to pay full price.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Has 'Cashed Out' and Reportedly Earned Around $270,000, Fans Believe
articles.summary: Analysis of overnight cryptocurrency transactions points to the prolific GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out" of their meme coin, earning around $270,000 in the process.
articles.body:
Analysis of overnight cryptocurrency transactions points to the prolific GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out" of their meme coin, earning around $270,000 in the process.

That's according to reliable GTA watcher and crypto analyst Vice Cit , who previously posted evidence that strongly suggested the leaking antics of "Cyberleek" were part of a cryptocurrency scheme , rather than their claimed excuse of it being a protest against the death of physical media.

Every video posted by the person or persons known as Cyberleek has pointed to a website where fans could pay to vote on further leaks using the leaker's own cryptocurrency. These leaks have since increased in frequency over the past few days, and also escalated in terms of the content they showed — revealing full frontal nudity in one recent video, and then finally beginning to spoil the game's story in the latest clip posted to date .

The rapid release of more leaks, as well as Rockstar's own impending official reveal of gameplay footage via Netflix, suggested to some fans that Cyberleek was getting ready to make their move and earn whatever money they could before interest waned and their currency inevitably collapsed.

Indeed, this now appears to be the case, with Cyberleek apparently pocketing all the currency's trading fees and transferring them into at least two other sources overnight, ready for withdrawal. Vice Cit has a detailed log of where the money went, up to a point, but not enough to help identify who was actually behind it all. The fact that multiple withdrawal methods were allegedly used could point to multiple people being behind Cyberleek, Vice Cit speculated, though this cannot be confirmed.

"The original setup of this whole project (the CYBERLEEK token, the website, and the file uploads) was around $29,000 at the time of my first investigation," Vice Cit wrote. "Which means the person or group behind this leak profited around $241,000 if this is where this all ends. Not an amount to completely dismiss but is it really 'risk your freedom money'?

"I personally believe the leaker expected to make much more from this project and the watermark messaging in the most recent clips feels kind of panicky. As the coin continued to drop over the last 24 hours and the public started to lose interest I believe the leaker made the choice to cash out."

And then there's the million dollar (or $241,000) question: Are the GTA 6 leaks over? There's no reason why Cyberleek couldn't release more footage, and no suggestion they were close to getting caught. Indeed, it would be the ultimate test of Cyberleek actually caring about their stated cause of physical media if they continued posting even now. Time will tell, though at the time of writing Rockstar is now just hours from taking center stage.

articles.title: State of Decay 3 Announces Closed Beta Playtests Later This Year
articles.summary: State of Decay 3 fans will have the chance to play the game later this year via a closed beta.
articles.body:
State of Decay 3 fans will have the chance to play the game later this year via a closed beta.

Undead Labs has confirmed that it will hold a closed beta for State of Decay 3 before the end of 2026. Exact dates weren't given, but interested fans can sign up now by clicking here and filling out the required information. The studio also held an alpha earlier this year, which reportedly resulted in actionable feedback to improve the game. The team noted that the alpha allowed them to improve combat, cosmetics, visuals, and movement, resulting in a better product. The beta will only allow more opportunities to improve the game, according to Undead Labs.

“We’re going to be expanding our alpha and then closed beta to more players over time, this is our largest map ever and with untethered multiplayer, we really need to take the opportunities to stress-test and fine-tune,” said Kevin Patzelt, Creative Director at Undead Labs. “If you don’t get access right away, rest assured there will be more opportunities throughout the year for players familiar and brand new to the series.”

State of Decay 3 has been in the works since at least 2020, when the game was announced at the Xbox Series X/S reveal event. The project went quiet for a number of years, but was re-revealed in 2024 and is now planned for release sometime in 2027 . It's been a long road, and it hasn't been an easy one. Undead Labs is also splitting away from Xbox, as part of the platform's big reset. Xbox underwent a massive restructuring earlier this summer , leading to extensive layoffs and multiple studios being sold off or released to go independent.

Undead Labs is in the process of transitioning out of Xbox, though it's currently unclear what the studio's new path is, such as acquisition by another company or forging its own path. Additionally, it has been reported that Undead Labs will not be obligated to bring State of Decay 3 to Xbox Game Pass once it leaves Xbox. However, the blog post announcing the closed beta noted that the game is still planned for a Game Pass release. So, I guess we'll just have to wait and see what happens.

State of Decay 3 will release on Xbox Series X/S, PS5, and PC next year.

articles.title: Why Humble Bundle Is a Great Place to Buy Digital Comics
articles.body:
If you buy through our links, IGN may earn an affiliate commission. Learn more .

In the era of digital media, amassing a huge comic book collection is easier than ever, but it also comes with its share of challenges. File management and storage can be a pain, your comics can be split between several platforms that have different means of access, and building your collection one comic at a time can get expensive fast.

Humble Bundle can help solve those problems. If you’re already familiar with Humble, it’s probably because of their video game offers. But they also have and software , including comic books. And just like their video game offerings, they specialize in variety, flexibility, and getting the best bang for your buck.

For the uninitiated, the way Humble Bundle works is right there in the name: They sell bundles of content together that have some kind of link. That could mean books from the same publisher, like this Humanoids Megabundle . Or it could mean books with similar origins, like the Disney Masters bundle .

These bundles can have dozens of books included, but for a fraction of the price they’d cost individually. For example, the Disney Masters bundle (which has comics and graphic novels starring Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck, Goofy, and Uncle Scrooge) includes 48 comics valued at over $1,000 total, but you can get the full bundle for as little as $25, or basically 52 cents per comic.

The final amount you pay is actually up to you, though. Many bundles have tiers where you can pay less to get a smaller number of comics. Using the Disney Masters example again, you could choose to pay $5 for a three-book version of the bundle, or you could pay $15 for a nine-book version.

It’s tough to beat that level of flexibility and sheer value, making Humble Bundle a great choice for those wanting to buy comics at a great price. Plus, with so many titles included in each bundle, it gives you a chance to find new books you never would have tried otherwise. Which leads us to our next point.

When you’re limited to buying one book at a time, it can make finding new comics tough. You want to know you’re getting value for money, so it’s easy to fall into a pattern where you stick to headliner releases or franchises you’re already familiar with.

Buying with Humble Bundle addresses that problem. Bundles often include a mix of different writers, illustrators, and genres, giving you the chance to try a wide variety of styles. It allows you to discover things you might never have considered or even heard of.

Bundles will often include a mixture of heavy hitters and smaller comics, letting you have the best of both worlds. Humble's latest comic offerings include bundles like Dynamite Comics' Miniseries, Quick Hits and Speedy Reads book bundle which is filled with mini-adventures, and Image Comics' Image in the '20s: A Megabundle , to name a couple.

It’s no secret that superhero comics are the most popular. There’s a reason why Marvel and DC have become household names. Those are fun and all, but there are so many other types of comics out there too. You’re really missing out if you just stick to the most famous franchises.

Humble Bundle has selections from a bunch of different publishers of various sizes. That includes bundles like One Shots & Fast Reads , which has Image Comics selections like Jack Kirby’s Silver Star and Grant Morrison’s Nameless, to Dynamite Comics' mini-adventures, featuring stories with classic heroes like John Carter and the queen of pin-up, Bettie Page.

That’s only accounting for the currently active bundles, too. New bundles with a wide range of options are consistently rotating in. You never know what the next bundle will bring, which is part of the fun.

One of the headaches of building a catalog of digital comic books is the number of platforms and apps you have to account for. Your access to the book you bought can be blocked unless you use that specific platform, meaning you have to remember which book is connected to which account.

This is a form of DRM (digital rights management), which is intended to protect copyright holders. But for you, the user, it means you have to jump through hoops to read what you bought. And it can mean you don’t really own the things you buy, since your access can be restricted or rescinded at a moment’s notice.

Humble’s bundles don’t require subscriptions and often include DRM-free downloads, which means that after you buy a bundle, you get PDF, EPUB, or CBZ files which you can directly download. Whichever type you decide to use, the important thing is that you get to keep those comics. They’re yours forever.

To be clear, not every bundle is DRM-free. Under the description of each bundle, you’ll see a group of icons. If that bundle is DRM-free, there’s a book icon that says “Use on Any Device.” If not, there’s a key icon that says “Redeem on Other Platform” and the bundle description will provide more details.

Humble has always been extremely supportive of charities, for which it has raised more than $280 million since being founded in 2010 . It donates a portion of every sale to charity, but you can also pay extra money for your bundle and choose whether to give that money to the comics’ creators, Humble Bundle, its partners, or a charity of your choice.

Each month, Humble chooses a different charity to feature. That charity receives a portion of Humble Choice membership dues and the proceeds of individual bundles (unless you choose a different charity). The featured charity for August is the international ocean conservation group Oceana, while previous charities include Make-A-Wish, The Trevor Project, and No Kid Hungry.

On the listing for each bundle, you can see how much has been donated to charity thanks to purchases of that bundle. There are multiple currently available bundles that have contributed more than $10,000 of donations each. And everyone wants to put more good into the world, right? So why not do it while getting to read dozens of comics for cheap? Win-win.

Why Humble Bundle Is a Great Place to Buy Comics

When it comes to buying digital comics, Humble Bundle is the best option for sheer value, discovery, and flexibility. It combines extremely low prices, flexible downloads, a variety of titles, and a consistently rotating selection so there’s always something new for you to check out without breaking the bank.

It’s perfect for newcomers wanting to get their feet wet and see what kinds of comics they vibe with, as well as hardcore fans looking to take their collection to the next level without having to shell out hundreds of dollars at a time. Regardless of your experience level, you can discover new titles you never knew existed.

The next time you’re looking for new comics, are you going to give Humble Bundle a look? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Nvidia Fails to Mention Gaming in Earnings Report, and Now I Wonder When the RTX 6080 Will Ever Come Out
articles.summary: Nvidia released its Q2 2027 earnings report yesterday, and while it's obvious the company is making a ton of money on data centers – up 106% from this time last year – the company didn't mention gaming once.
articles.body:
Nvidia released its Q2 2027 earnings report yesterday , and while it's obvious the company is making a ton of money on data centers – up 106% from this time last year – the company didn't mention gaming once.

That shouldn't be too surprising. After all, Team Green dropped the gaming category from its earnings report last quarter , moving it into 'edge computing.' In that category this quarter, the only time 'RTX' shows up is when the RTX Spark, launched at Computex 2026 , was mentioned. I've had the chance to play with the RTX Spark-equipped Surface a couple times at events since then, and while it's definitely capable of gaming, systems with that chipset are absolutely geared more toward local AI workloads than playing Alan Wake 2 .

At least part of the reason gaming wasn't mentioned, I suspect, is because we're smack dab in the middle of a GPU generation right now. The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 and the rest of the Blackwell GeForce lineup came out about a year and a half ago, so it makes sense that gaming is a bit quiet. But, with how much cash AI is making Nvidia, and with the RAM crisis – which Nvidia absolutely contributes to – driving graphics card prices through the roof, I can't help but wonder when we're going to actually see new GPUs.

I've seen rumors that the RTX 6080 likely won't be launching until the end of 2027 at the earliest, which, if true, would make this one of the longest graphics generations in memory. As early as February 2026, a report from The Information suggested the RTX 60 series would be delayed beyond 2027, and we still haven't got the mid-generation 'Super' refresh that we typically see halfway through each graphics generation.

Instead, most of the gaming news out of Nvidia this year has been around software. The company previewed the controversial DLSS 5 back in March, which will use gen AI to essentially re-draw games . But even beyond that, the company just released a new ray reconstruction model as part of DLSS 4.5, which is genuinely awesome, and there have been incremental upgrades to multi-frame generation throughout the year that have made that technology much less jarring.

At the end of the day, I'm not sure if it's a bad thing if new graphics cards take a while to actually come out. If there's one thing that rings true about pretty much every hardware launch this year, it's that they've been overpriced due to the RAM shortage. Nvidia's cards have carried a higher premium with every launch, so it's hard to imagine just how expensive a flagship graphics card launching in 2026 or 2027 would actually be.

My advice, then, would be to brace yourself for a few more years without an upgrade. Hopefully game developers will use this time to make sure games run a bit smoother on older hardware. The good news is that some of the best games this year have been successful there, like Crimson Desert and Forza Horizon 6 , which run well on basically anything. But there are still games like Star Wars Zero Company and Halo: Campaign Evolved which all but demand newer GPUs. Hopefully, we see more of the former than the latter in the jam-packed second half of 2026.

articles.title: Rockstar Games and Florida Officials Are Having Conversations to Turn Miami Into Vice City IRL for GTA 6's Marketing Campaign
articles.summary: Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing campaign.
articles.body:
Florida officials and Rockstar Games are having conversations to turn parts of Miami into Vice City for Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing campaign.

As initially reported by The Miamian , Miami-Dade County has had formal conversations with Rockstar Games about a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami to promote the upcoming game. The report initially noted that Rockstar was the one that approached Miami-Dade with its ideas, but the article was later edited to clarify the city was actually the one who submitted a pitch deck.

While no plans are officially in place yet, the ideas pitched by the city are wide-ranging, ambitious, and likely absurdly expensive. One such idea includes transforming a section of Miami International Airport to serve as a "welcome" area for Vice City, complete with Vice City signage, limited edition luggage tags, themed luggage carts, a photo backdrop, and even a display aircraft wrapped in the game's purple color scheme.

Officials also proposed various activations around Miami's beaches, parks, and ports, creating unique events with DJs, food, exotic vehicles, photo ops, drone shows, murals, and much more. Outside of actual events, there are even ideas to have Rockstar take over the city's busses and trains with Vice City branding on the actual locomotives and stations associated with them. On the smaller side, there was also a pitch for Vice City-branded manhole covers and utility boxes.

The city created a number of proposals that would actually permanently help Miami in the long term, such as the creation of more bus shelters, quality of life improvements for its parks, and more. One of the more unique suggestions included the construction of a "radio lab" at a library in downton Miami. This would give visitors access to recording and editing equipment to produce music, podcasts, and more.

In a statement to The Miamian, Carlos Suarez, a spokesperson for Miami-Dade Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, confirmed that they've had conversations with Rockstar Games, but there are no concrete plans in place at the moment.

“Nothing has been formally agreed to or approved, and any idea would have to go through the appropriate review and approval process," said Suarez. "Given Miami-Dade's clear influence on the game, we think there could be a unique opportunity to generate revenue for the County while showcasing Miami-Dade to a massive audience.”

It wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar uses the city of Miami to promote GTA 6 as part of its expansive marketing campaign, but it seems unlikely that it would go forth with all of these ideas. Not only are they expensive, but they may not all make sense for what Rockstar is envisioning for its advertising campaign.

The final marketing push for GTA 6 will ramp up today when Rockstar premieres an extended look at the game on Netflix . If you don't have Netflix or simply don't have time to watch, IGN will be doing a live blog with all of the big news from Rockstar's reveal. Additionally, a few new details were revealed yesterday including tidbits about specific gameplay mechanics and Rockstar doubling its size in order to produce GTA 6 .

articles.title: Helldivers 2 Boss Happy That GTA 6 Is Skipping PC at Launch and There's No Online Right Away
articles.summary: Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried.
articles.body:
Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases. But according to the CEO of Helldivers 2 developer Arrowhead, there are two very good reasons why developers shouldn’t be too worried.

Speaking to IGN, Arrowhead boss Shams Jorjani said that the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 at launch, as well as the absence of whatever the next generation of GTA Online looks like, means there’s reason to believe games like Helldivers 2 retain their own space.

“Rockstar makes ridiculous, high-effort stuff and it's awesome that games like this get made,” Jorjani said. “On a selfish level I'm happy it’s not hitting PC right away, and that online isn’t dropping at launch. It means Helldivers 2 gets to keep crushing it in our own space, and is also why it won’t be the all consuming behemoth everyone’s worried about.

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

“Everyone in the industry right now is constantly pivoting strategies and obsessing over early player feedback just to survive. But Rockstar has the brand power to confidently take their time and run their classic play. They have the confidence and freedom to spend a decade doing things the old-school way because they know the core game will deliver. It’s going to raise the bar for sure.”

Of course, Helldivers 2 is also out on console (it’s a PlayStation Studios game and Sony owns the Helldivers IP), but the explosive co-op action game is particularly strong on Steam, where it retains a loyal and sizeable audience of fans even now, two-and-a-half years after launch.

You’d image that the launch of GTA 6 will have an impact on even PC games, but perhaps long-running Steam games that revolve around online play will prove more resilient than others. Let's remember: GTA 6 is a single-player game at launch. There's no online mode at all this November.

GTA 6 is also set for launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S only, which in 2026 feels like an odd release strategy but is in keeping with Rockstar’s playbook. Jorjani touches on this in his comment — Rockstar is perhaps one of the few video game developers around that can guarantee success even skipping PC. GTA 6 is just that big of a deal. There’s nothing like it.

Be sure to check out IGN’s GTA 6 official gameplay reveal live blog , where we’ll bring you all the news across the internet on today’s Netflix exclusive and beyond.
