articles.title: Playdate Manufacturer Panic Is Passing Tariff Refunds to Customers
articles.summary: Panic's Playdate, a crank-powered handheld gaming system, launched all the way back in 2022, but last year it fell victim to the same tariffs that hit many gaming products. And, now that the Supreme Court has ordered the government to refund those fees, Panic is forwarding those refunds to the customers that actually paid them.
articles.body:
Panic's Playdate , a crank-powered handheld gaming system, launched all the way back in 2022, but last year it got hit with the same tariffs as many gaming products. Now that the Supreme Court has ordered the government to refund those fees, Panic is forwarding those refunds to the customers that actually paid them.

The company started sending out emails, spotted on LinkedIn and Reddit , informing customers that they'd be getting a tariff refund sent to their original payment method. The refund itself isn't much — the highest one I've seen is a $25 refund — but when it's attached to a handheld that costs $250 now and $179 at launch, it's a pretty decent percentage.

If you bought one of these fun little handhelds when the tariffs were active, you should be automatically getting an email notifying you of the refund. If not, you should be able to reach out to help@play.date to figure out what's going on.

Ideally, we'd see more companies refunding tariffs now that the refunds have started flowing from the governmen, but there are definitely companies that are holding on to those fees. Even Nintendo has refused to issue refunds to Switch 2 customers , arguing that gamers got exactly what they paid for. Hopefully, the Playdate manufacturers can set a decent example for other companies to follow.

After all, tarrifs aren't the only thing causing prices to go up lately. Since the beginning of 2026, the RAMpocalypse has had a much bigger impact on prices , and that probably won't let up any time soon. The way I see it, passing on at least some savings to customers now that prices are solidly out of control is the least manufacturers could do.

articles.title: The LEGO Mario Minifigure Sets Look Like a Much-Needed ‘Reset’ for the Mario Theme
articles.summary: For years, LEGO's Mario-themed sets for kids have felt lackluster. With the recently announced sets, it looks like that's changing.
articles.body:
LEGO has announced its first sets based around a new group of Mario minifigures , and they look pretty great. The company has just released pictures of the boxes these sets will come in, and, uh, I kind of want these sets just for the boxes?

The boxes are bright and bold and colorful, all decked out in the same red and blue shades that make Mario the recognizable mascot as he is. I mean, just look at this box for the Fire Mario & Bower’s Castle set. It’s perfect .

This new line of Mario sets is something of a reset ( ba-dum-tss ) for the LEGO Mario theme. Mario and LEGO have years of history together, including plenty of awesome Nintendo LEGO sets . But the overwhelming majority of the Mario sets belonged to a play-focused LEGO Super Mario theme .

These sets were based around a big (for LEGO), boxy, non-minifigure Mario that could “interact” with the environmental elements you built. That interaction was limited to sounds and music coming out of the Mario figure, along with simple animations that played on a tiny LED screen built into his chest.

I got to try out a handful of these sets when LEGO added a boxy Luigi figure to the mix. Let’s just say they didn’t wow me. They were clearly designed for young kids, but I had young kids at the time, and they didn’t want to play with the sets for more than a couple minutes, either.

Those Mario sets just weren’t very fun. And because they were designed for the weird boxy Mario figures to "interact" with, they didn't look very good, either.

Based on looks alone, that's all changing with these new Mario minifigure-based sets LEGO has just announced. They look much more fun. They’re still primarily intended for kids to play with them – just look at the suggested ages on the packaging; LEGO sets for adults they are not. But they're minifigure-scale, and they include plenty of "regular" interactive elements of the kind found on many LEGO sets. The main difference is that they don’t have the gimmicky interactivity of the boxy Mario. And I think that's going to make all the difference.

LEGO Super Mario: Mario's Beach Adventures

LEGO Super Mario: Fire Luigi vs. Koopa Troopa Battle

LEGO Super Mario: Luigi & Bowser Jr.'s Race

LEGO Super Mario: Yoshi at Mario's House

LEGO Super Mario: Bowser's Rumbling Race

LEGO Super Mario: Fire Mario & Bowser's Castle

In other words, they’re regular LEGO sets, just like the incredibly successful Star Wars and Harry Potter themes, but they're based on the wonderful world of the Mushroom Kingdom. That’s all LEGO needed to do to make Mario sets fun in the first place. And as for the minifigure versions of the Mario crew? They look great.

For the first time ever, I’m optimistic about the upcoming Mario LEGO sets for kids.

For more, check out our list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Alienware Just Released the World's First 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology
articles.summary: The best monitor for both gaming and workstation productivity is now shipping.
articles.body:
Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account). This monitor has potential to be an outstanding performer in both gaming and workstation use thanks to its unparalleled text clarity, and it comes with a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in.

New Release: Alienware AW3926QW 39" 5K OLED Gaming Monitor

39" Alienware AW3926QW 5K RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Gaming Monitor

The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.

Tandem and RGB stripe technologies aside, the AW3926QW is also Alienware's first 5K OLED monitor. With an impressive 5120 x 2160 resolution, this 39" monitor boasts a pixel density of 143ppi. That's even sharper than an already impressive 32" 4K monitor, with its pixel density of 138ppi. A 39" monitor is pretty wide, so the AW3926QW employs a 1500R curve to balance it out. 1500R is pretty moderate as far as curved monitors go, so although you'll be able to see the entire monitor within your field of view, it won't significantly distort peripheral images.

OLED monitors are known for their extreme fast response time and perfect black levels, making them ideal for gaming. The AW3926QW ups the ante with its 165Hz refresh rate at 4K and support for AMD FreeSync Premium Pro and NVIDIA G-Sync compatibility. It has both DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1 ports so you'll be able to connect it to just about any modern day graphics card without the need for adapters.

Alienware also backs the monitor up with a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in.

articles.title: Kingdom Hearts' Story Has Gotten So Complex That Tetsuya Nomura Says Square Enix Hired a Loremaster to Keep the Plot Cohesive
articles.summary: The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its story cohesive.
articles.body:
The lore of Kingdom Hearts is so expansive that Tetsuya Nomura says Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep its story cohesive.

Kingdom Hearts IV is officially set for a late 2027 release. In the lead-up to its highly anticipated launch, fans have been returning to previous games in the series, to the point where a collection of Kingdom Hearts titles became one of the highest-selling games on Steam following an extended gameplay trailer shown at D23 in July.

In total, there are 13 games in the Kingdom Hearts franchise, which have been released on a bevy of different platforms over the years. That’s a lot to play through, not to mention a lot of story beats to keep track of as you go.

Kingdom Hearts 4 - Official Announcement Images

This isn’t a player-specific problem; even the developers find themselves getting lost from time to time, as revealed by series creator Tetsuya Nomura during an August 2026 interview with Famitsu . In fact, the storyline is so convoluted that Square Enix hired a loremaster to keep everything cohesive and explain the plot to Disney.

“As the Kingdom Hearts series has continued, the number of characters has inevitably increased, and the story has become more complex,” Nomura said. “For example, with the newly announced anime series , the number of external people involved in the Kingdom Hearts series has increased, and explaining the settings and scenarios each time has become quite difficult.

“Fortunately, the staff working on the ‘χ series’ had someone who meticulously compiled and organized the settings of past Kingdom Hearts series in an easy-to-understand way, and he was also in charge of explaining the scenarios and settings to Disney. In fact, at the beginning of Kingdom Hearts IV's development, Disney requested that he compile the materials, so he officially joined the Kingdom Hearts IV team as a proofreader.

Nomura says this "proofreader" was in charge of communicating the overarching story to Disney. He's a popular staff member due to how thorough his is, as he breaks down story beats, characters, and lore using visual diagrams.

"He is well-liked because he explains things to Disney as clearly as possible, using diagrams and such. His role internally is to proofread the script," he continued. "He checks to make sure there are no inconsistencies between the current script and past settings. He was especially suitable for this project because the χ series is deeply involved. Some people might mistakenly think he's in charge of composition, but it's actually ‘proofreading.’”

Nomura’s answer also revealed an integral connection between Kingdom Hearts IV and the χ titles, a series of prequel games set during the Age of Fairy Tales. These games were primarily available on web browsers and mobile devices, but Nomura says that “even if you haven't played the smartphone version, don't worry, their personalities are depicted within [Kingdom Hearts IV]."

The fact that even Disney themselves needed a loremaster to help explain the Kingdom Hearts story is a hilarious anecdote; the plot is famously convoluted and overwhelming, to the point where we at IGN felt the need to make a video explaining the lore in just five minutes .

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: 69 New GTA 6 Gameplay Details We Saw at Rockstar HQ
articles.summary: We visited Rockstar to check out GTA 6, and these are the 69 brand new details we saw while watching live gameplay.
articles.body:
We recently had the opportunity to visit Grand Theft Auto 6 developer Rockstar North to talk to co-studio head Rob Nelson and watch him play through an extended section of GTA 6. Over the course of the demonstration, we saw how a reimagined Vice City has been brought to life as Rob took us on a detailed tour of Rockstar’s brand-new open world. And there were a lot of details to dig into.

From how dual protagonists Jason and Lucia’s dynamic will evolve over the course of the story to how the act of stealing cars has been completely reinvented, here are 69 brand new GTA 6 gameplay details we learned during our trip to Rockstar.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

1. As with GTA 5, you can switch between the game’s leads at any time while exploring the open world. While designed to remain available as often as possible, switching may be disabled at certain points in the story.

2. When playing as one character, you can do things solo, or you can summon the other to help out with open-world activities or to simply hang out. To do that, you can call or text your partner in crime at any time, and they’ll travel to your location.

3. When traveling in a car together, you can switch seats and allow for the other character to drive if you fancy a little break and want to just chill out with the radio playing. During car chases or escapes, you can choose to sit in the passenger seat and shoot while the other drives.

4. If you’re out on your own for most of a day, you might get a text from Jason or Lucia reminding you to lock up the house when you get back late, or letting you know they’re heading to bed. Ignoring these messages may result in your relationship being negatively affected.

5. At the beginning of the story, Jason and Lucia want to pursue a romantic relationship. Whether this ends up happening is up to you, though. This is managed by spending time together outside of missions, as the critical story path may not provide a sufficient amount of time for their love to blossom.

6. Ways to strengthen the couple’s bond include exploring Leonida, going shopping, visiting hair salons, or exercising as a pair, and, of course, committing robberies together — this is GTA, after all. There are almost certainly plenty of other couples' activities to do, too.

7. No matter how tense things get between the pair, they’ll still have each other's backs, even if they're not close romantically, as the narrative running through the main missions requires this. How close they are at certain points does affect how their story will play out, though.

8. There are no specific gameplay benefits earned by building a strong romantic connection, meaning romance is completely optional and predominantly a roleplaying decision for players to make

9. If you do want to engage with that side of things, though, you can hold hands while out and about with a pull of the right trigger. Other little touches include being able to hold doors open for each other.

Safehouses, Cosmetics, and Physical Stats

10. Jason and Lucia can live in the same safehouse together, and each operate on their own schedules to make their behaviour in the world feel as believable as possible.

11. GTA 6’s safehouses are more comparable to Red Dead Redemption 2’s camps than the series’ traditional houses, meaning other people could also pop in and out. One home we saw even belonged to someone other than Jason and Lucia.

12. These bases are designed to be more interactive than their equivalents from any other GTA. Like in Red Dead Redemption 2, you’ll be able to shorten or shave your hair and facial hair (new styles will still need to be cut at a salon or barber).

13. Multiple personal vehicles can be owned by each character and kept at safehouses. These have working trunks, and you can store a change of clothes and weapons in them to aid with fighting and escaping the law.

14. As is the norm with GTA, hair salons and clothing stores can be found throughout the open world, but each will now have exclusive items and signature hairstyles to encourage you to visit different ones.

15. As well as cosmetics, Jason and Lucia’s appearance can change depending on which activities you engage with. Going to the gym increases their muscularity and strength, but overeating will make them gain weight. Eating does provide a substantial boost to a character’s health, though. Each of these activities can be performed solo or as a couple.

16. Nelson described the map as being “very big”, though no definitive size was given. Each district is populated with buildings and people that are styled to fit the culture of their locations.

17. The map displayed on the pause screen is much more detailed than previous GTA games, with satellite imagery replacing the previous rudimentary “Google Maps” appearance of the blocks and streets.

18. Exploration is rewarded, and so there is encouragement to spend time away from story missions. Events and missions are not limited to those found through objective or map icons.

19. Random events will occur naturally in the world. An example of one such interaction is the option to give some pills to a questionable lawyer sitting in a dumpster. Grant him the drugs, and he’ll lend you some legal advice.

20. You can fast travel using a taxi app called Ryde Me. If you’re in the car with another passenger, you can talk to them and have full conversations over the course of the drive.

21. Don’t want to spend time listening to the general public? Well, fear not, as the radio is here to save you. In typical GTA fashion, there are both radio and TV advertisements to be amused by, with more of both than in any prior game in the series. We saw ones for depression drug “Angstipan” and The Prairie Sandwich, which contains a light 30,000 calories.

22. You can also distract yourself by browsing the apps on your phone. These include the returning Instagram parody, Snapmatic. This time, though, you can’t post your own photos due to Jason and Lucia being a couple on the run and not wanting to leave a digital footprint. Instead, you can lurk, follow other accounts, and browse general content on it.

23. The phone menu no longer pops up in the bottom right corner of the frame. Instead, the camera now zooms in on Jason or Lucia’s hand when they pull it out of their pocket, with the phone being an actual in-game item rather than a part of the HUD. It’s a similar presentation to how Red Dead Redemption 2 shifts to first-person when Arthur cleans one of his pistols.

24. There are many open-world activities to engage with, including, but not limited to: playing pool, mini golf, kayaking, going to the zoo, scuba diving, parachute jumping, and going to the gym.

25. When at the zoo, or out in the wild, you can study animals, and each new one you find will be checked off a list. This system is derived from Red Dead Redemption 2.

26. Dogs can be petted (or scolded, if you’re a heartless human).

27. Aside from animals, there’s also the human wildlife of Leonida to observe, with NPCs consisting of a far greater variation in body shape and height than any previous Rockstar game. Depending on their size, the game dynamically retargets animations so that they interact with the environment and other characters in as realistic a way as possible.

28. You can interact with NPCs using an evolved version of the system from Red Dead Redemption 2, with conversation options available when a character is targeted while your gun is holstered. Greet and taunt are both introductory prompts, as well as defuse and provoke if someone is being aggressive toward you.

29. You can also stand by NPCs and listen to their conversations. They’ll notice if you’re eavesdropping, though, and may confront you if they think you’ve overstepped a boundary. The same goes for if an NPC thinks you’ve been following them for an uncomfortable amount of time.

30. Sometimes, though, an NPC may just choose to initiate violence with Jason or Lucia, and your protagonists are not the only civilians in Vice City and its surrounding area who are carrying weapons on their person.

31. These conversations and interactions can trigger activities, which create an organic experience alongside the more traditional player-selected missions. Even ambient dialogue can create emergent events.

32. Jason and Lucia can spontaneously propose nearby activities or jobs, allowing an intended trip to turn into a different emergent activity, should you agree to their idea.

33. To help locate useful items and avoid police in the world, you can use the new Focus system that highlights things of interest in the world.

Police, Wanted Levels, and Your Criminal Profile

34. For the Wanted Level system to kick in, a crime must first be witnessed by an NPC, or an alarm triggered.

35. The dispatched officers will then get specific information about the reported incident and respond to the area of the crime. The ‘hot area’ can remain marked on the map even after Jason and Lucia have left the area. Police can continue to search at that scene for a period of time until it cools down.

36. GTA 6 sees the return of the six-star wanted level after GTA 5 changed to five stars. One star of heat is intended to be relatively easy to escape, while six offers that classic high-chaos GTA getaway experience.

37. At three stars and higher, it can be hard to escape if you’re in the city unless you have a very fast vehicle. This is due to tighter, narrower streets and the high-density population of people and traffic. Rather than risking a car chase, alleys and off-shoots from streets can be used to flee on foot. GTA 6 has reworked movement, including running, jumping, and climbing, to make this all feel smoother.

38. When wanted, the police can learn what you look like, as well as what you’re wearing. These details are indicated by different icons that appear under your wanted level on the HUD. Changing your hair will remove the appearance icon, as you now look physically different, but the police still know what you’re wearing and be able to track you using those details. Putting on glasses or a new hat isn’t enough to disrupt that information, either; you’ll need to change into a whole new outfit, hence why keeping a fresh set of clothes in your car’s trunk is a great idea.

39. Equipping masks during a crime, and then removing them as you escape, can prevent a description of your appearance even making its way to the police, even if you’re caught by CCTV.

40. But the cops can also know what vehicle you’re driving, so abandoning a recognised vehicle and entering a different one is also another way of reducing heat.

41. During a police search, Lucia and Jason can opt to split up to divert police attention if it’s been reported that the suspects are a couple. You can tell the other character to flee during an encounter and take the heat for yourself. If the pair are separated while escaping, you’ll later get a text from the other partner once the coast is clear.

42. The classic white wanted stars will be displayed as hollow outlines if the police don’t know what you look like, meaning as long as you leave the area of the crime without drawing attention to yourself, you should be in the clear.

43. If either Jason or Lucia is arrested, the traditional “Busted” screen appears, and you’ll respawn into the world, even if the other is still escaping from a crime scene.

44. Not all confrontations have to result in the police being summoned, though. Some scenarios can be defused without violence, such as aiming but not firing a gun at an NPC, causing them to flee.

45. Sometimes escalation is designed to be unavoidable, though, such as in some story missions. Overall, a hit-and-run approach is encouraged, with the idea that you get in and out of crime scenes before the police arrive and it all kicks off.

46. Get yourself into a shootout, and you’ll now be able to incapacitate enemies as an alternative to just killing them. Aim for the arm or leg to put them down non-lethally, or if you’re accurate enough, shoot their weapon out of their hand to disarm them.

47. Slow motion moments of particularly impressive violence will be showcased from a cinematic camera angle, much like Red Dead Redemption 2 highlighted some of Arthur’s best shots.

48. The Criminal Profile system is GTA 6’s version of Red Dead Redemption 2’s honour system, but distinct from it inasmuch as there isn’t a clear and defined “right or wrong” morality to the way you play.

49. A consistent pattern of behaviour might affect how the world and the people within it react to you when free-roaming, as well as how the main story may play out. Actions involving unnecessary moments of violence or causing more mayhem than called for can contribute to your profile. Additionally, acts that contribute to being a good citizen – such as throwing away your own trash – also adjust your Criminal Profile.

50. Crucially, crimes committed when on missions and robberies, or situations when you’re forced to use aggression, won’t necessarily shift the Criminal Profile.

51. Rockstar intends for money to matter more to the story than in previous GTA games, and you’ll sometimes be required to raise a certain amount of capital in order for the flow of main missions to continue.

52. The main ways to make money include boosting and selling cars, holding up businesses, robbing stores, and executing bank heists.

53. Robbery targets can be approached by either Jason or Lucia solo, or as a couple. Doing a job together counts towards growing their relationship.

54. Jobs can be executed in different ways, as greed vs. speed becomes a huge factor. It may be quicker to use some explosives to blow open a safe, but that will damage the loot inside. Take a little longer to search around the business for the safe combination, and you’ll earn more money, but at the risk of law enforcement turning up mid-heist.

55. Police presence can even build outside of a store or bank and wait for you to leave. Thankfully, a lot of robbery locations offer alternative routes of escape, such as a back door.

56. Stolen goods will then need to be sold to a fence, as, once again, GTA 6 takes a leaf out of Red Dead Redemption 2’s book. Fences exist for items such as jewellery, but also for cars.

57. A fence looking for cars may also give you information, such as the code for a police impound that’s home to vehicles ready to be boosted and cashed in on.

58. Getting behind the wheel of a stolen vehicle won’t be as simple as in past GTA games, though. Cars are now categorised by a tier system, with more expensive models proving a much tougher challenge to get into.

59. When approaching a parked car that’s taken your fancy, the first thing you’ll want to do is use the new WAINK (yes, really) phone app to scan the vehicle. This will tell you how much it’s worth, the cost of registering it as a personal vehicle, whether it’s locked or alarmed, and if it has a tracker.

60. Different tiers and types of vehicle require different tools of entry, such as a simple slim jim for older, less secure cars, or a technologically advanced key cloner for modern, prestige vehicles. Some cars will be inaccessible early in the game because the necessary tools are not acquired until later in the story.

61. Any car that has an occupant in the driver’s seat can be stolen, though, with carjacking working just how you remember it from previous GTA games.

62. Any cars you’ve stolen will be worth less if delivered to a fence damaged. The challenge of delivering a pristine car is made harder by the narrower streets and denser traffic of GTA 6, which have both been designed with increased realism in mind.

63. Some vehicles will also be fitted with advanced trackers, which will alert the police to your location if you drive too slowly. This means you’ll either need to pick up the speed or abandon the car.

64. GTA 6’s story will include choices both big and small, with some minor decisions accumulating and resulting in larger consequences. Some major choices will result in significant and immediate change. Overall, the narrative has been designed to support repeat playthroughs.

65. Though Rockstar often prioritises directed storytelling when specific plot beats need to be delivered, the studio has attempted as much as possible with GTA 6 to connect open-world actions to each of its characters’ identities and their stories.

66. As much thought is given to gameplay choice within missions, too. We were shown a tower block mission which contained multiple escape routes, a mission where you could freely choose between being in the driving seat or shooting from beside it, and a police chase in which an optimal path to freedom was suggested, while also allowing other routes of escape.

67. Lucia’s ankle tag will play a notable part in the story and is key to how she and Jason are brought together. They each have dense backstories that are sometimes outright revealed, and other times only alluded to. Could a stronger relationship reveal hidden secrets?

68. The story is designed to reward spending time in the world rather than moving directly from mission to mission. Rockstar says it has blurred the lines between open world and main mission activities.

69. That trademark Rockstar satire and brand of comedy will run through the story and the larger world. It won’t rely heavily on specific political issues or memes, due to the long development cycle of the game potentially causing them to date quickly. The same can be said for contemporary slang, with the intention being that the characters’ dialogue remains as timeless as possible.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: ‘It’s a Big Map, a Very Big Map’ – GTA 6 Is Rockstar’s Most Complex World Yet
articles.summary: Rockstar explains how it has pushed current-gen technology to ensure GTA 6’s massive map is a step beyond Red Dead Redemption 2’s world.
articles.body:
When it comes to open-world games, and especially Rockstar’s, one of the biggest questions is always “how big is the map?” Well, when it comes to GTA 6 we now have a answer. Kind of.

The main stories of Rockstar games and the bombastic missions that they’re made up of are always a huge part of the allure of these now once-in-a-generation events, but there’s always plenty to do once those tales have ended. As with 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, it will be no different in GTA 6.

“There is a whole other world in Red Dead Redemption 2, yes. GTA 6 is very much like that,” Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North, told IGN in an exclusive interview. “There's a whole lot of stuff that you discover emergently that we're not necessarily directing you to through objectives or blips or icons on a map as well. If you take a bit of time and explore you will be rewarded – a lot. It’s a big map, a very big map.”

To create such a large playground to play in takes a huge amount of time and effort, though, as well as the tools to build them with. This is where the power of the current generation of consoles comes into the picture, with Rockstar now able to push things even further than Red Dead Redemption 2 was able to go when it launched on PS4 and Xbox One.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

“I think with Red Dead Redemption 2, we finally had the team and the tech and then took the time we needed to push the idea of making a fully realized consistent-feeling world further than we ever had,” Nelson explains. “With that game we took the time necessary to take advantage of that generation of hardware to maximize the quality of our open world population, design, and gameplay so that when you were riding from here to there in-game, you were constantly getting distracted and pulled in different directions. And then you could really get lost as that character in that place. That's when to me, these games can feel magical and create a sense of wonder that the world is alive – and you get these little shivers of ‘What’s happening?’

GTA 6 is a continuation of our team pushing in this direction – doing everything we possibly can to create the largest, deepest, most densely populated and complex world we have ever built for people to get lost in.”

One of the most noticeable improvements to the world of Leonida when compared to previous Grand Theft Auto locations, will be the people that populate. Thanks to the power of modern consoles, a far greater level of diversity will be seen when it comes to body shapes, height, and the way they move through Vice City and its surrounding areas.

“One of the coolest things about this game being developed from the ground up on this generation of hardware is taking advantage of all the memory that we have on the latest consoles combined with our teams’ experience doing this for so long together,” says Nelson.

“NPCs have more height differentiation and body shape differentiation than ever before, we could never have had this variety before because different body types had to share animation sets. So, if you had the same animation on the 5’6” person and the 6’2” person, they wouldn’t line up if they're fighting or sitting in cars—basically any interactions with each other or the environment. But on this game, the team worked out a system where they now retarget those animations on the fly. Now we have a huge variety of heights and shapes and it all works together because of what this team was able to pull off.”

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: ‘Is It Four Characters Now?’ — Rockstar Briefly Thought About Doubling the Number of GTA 6 Protagonists
articles.summary: Following GTA 5’s three playable characters, Rockstar considered putting four protagonists in GTA 6 before settling on its criminal couple.
articles.body:
Long before we knew that GTA 6 would be played from the perspective of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, many were wondering just how many playable characters Rockstar’s latest would include. And it turns out that the answer wasn’t always two.

Grand Theft Auto 5 charted a new direction for the series by increasing the number of characters to three, where there had always been just one. Red Dead Redemption 2 does have multiple protagonists, but can never be switched between in the style of GTA 5 due to story reasons. It begged the question of which direction the developer would go when first designing 6.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

IGN recently visited Rockstar North to speak with co-studio head Rob Nelson, who revealed discussions were had at one point in time regarding the number of characters increasing to four. But, ultimately, the team landed on one couple, with the bonds built between player and character at the foremost point of those discussions.

“As the narrative unfolds, we're quite conscious to try and make sure that players have enough time with each character,” says Nelson. “After doing GTA 5, we talked about different ideas of – do we do more characters? How do we follow up three characters? Is it four characters now? But we worried about diluting the amount of player time with each and therefore player connection with those characters. So we decided to step in this direction of two characters in a relationship.”

But then the question became: how do you make players feel like, ‘I love them both?’ Chemistry is a notoriously hard thing to do in any sort of entertainment. Either the characters and the actors that embody them have it – or they don't. Everyone involved worked at that pretty hard. I think we’ve got it. I think we’ve got enough reaction within our team internally to where they feel great as individuals and together.”

articles.title: ‘We Are Nervous!’ — Rockstar Knows the Pressure on GTA 6 to Be a Success
articles.summary: We asked Rockstar how it’s dealing with the pressure of ensuring GTA 6 is a success after so many years of development: ‘We are nervous!’
articles.body:
It feels like the whole world is waiting to play GTA 6. And Rockstar knows it.

Ahead of the extended look that just debuted on Netflix, IGN had the chance to visit the developer and talk with Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. Upon us mentioning just how each new Grand Theft Auto feels like a global cultural moment, he replies with a laugh, “No pressure.”

“I try not to think about it,” Nelson continues. “You’re aware of it, of course. But I think we just have to try and make something that we feel is innovating on what we’ve done previously, evolving it while still making it feel familiar.”

Rockstar knows that each and every scrap of information revealed about GTA 6 is analysed with a fine-tooth comb, and this recent extended look is certainly no different, as we’re given our biggest insight yet into the world, characters, and gameplay of this revisit to Vice City. It means each frame needs to be perfect, with every detail bound to be made into a list feature revealing new secrets about the game — exactly something we’ll be doing ourselves.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

“It’s a hard thing,” Nelson explains. “As much pressure as we feel externally, I don’t think it can compare to the pressure we put on ourselves as a team. Everyone wants things to be perfect. We are nervous! Nervous, of course, but also excited to see how people respond to this video and then ultimately the game. It is definitely a step forward in all respects for us – the size of the world, and how deep it feels. It’s a bit of a shock when you get in there, and you see the density of the traffic, the density of population, and the fidelity of their responses to you.”

While we don’t as of yet know just how many people have pre-ordered GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 launch, we do know that the majority of players have opted for the more expensive $100 ultimate edition than the standard one. The boss of the game’s publisher, Take-Two, has described that price as a “bargain” as “Rockstar Games is known for over-delivering.” You can see why Nelson and company may well be feeling that pressure.

articles.title: GTA 6 Exclusive Preview
articles.summary: We visited Rockstar HQ to watch the devs play GTA 6 – what we saw was like stepping into a parallel universe.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6. The most anticipated game of at least the last decade. And somehow, I'm sitting down at Rockstar North, about to watch co-studio head Rob Nelson play through 30 minutes of the game. It's a privilege only a handful of people have been granted. Holy shit. HOLY SHIT .

Half an hour later, it's crystal clear that this game will occupy every waking minute of my existence when it finally arrives this November. If you need to know just one thing about GTA 6, it's that you're going to spend so much time in it you'll probably be subject to Leonida taxes. When IGN was invited to enter the secretive halls of Rockstar North for an exclusive look, I suspected that the slice of gameplay would be designed to show off just how much GTA has grown and evolved since its last iteration launched 13 years ago. Even knowing that, the scope of what I saw is even more colossal than I was prepared for. Combined, the gameplay and Nelson revealed a new era for the series, one where everything that made us all fall in love with a life of crime is still there, but now it's set in a world so rich and ready to explore that it's not just a game; it's a parallel universe.

After watching the latest TV episode-length “Extended Look” ahead of its Netflix debut - can you imagine how many times I've nearly combusted keeping that secret from family and friends? - and another 30 minutes of live gameplay, I knew GTA 6 is going to be a multi-layered world of crime, exploration, side quests, and secrets that's more connected and finely tuned than any other game in the series. For a start, the setting of Leonida instantly feels more densely populated than anything we've seen before. Streets are full of NPCs hanging out, making conversation, and they're all ready to interact with Lucia or Jason in different ways. A quick peek at the giant map revealed an almost overwhelming amount of icons for stores, opportunities, and activities, and the trailers have given us a glimpse of even more. It's clear that this is going to be a playground that rewards exploration and that unguided adventures are now as much a part of the GTA 6 experience as the story, rather than just a clever backdrop. You can swap between the two protagonists at almost any point or explore the world together while you manage their stats with food buffs and workouts.

The biggest part of all the trailers so far has been Jason and Lucia and the connection between them. It's a real Bonnie and Clyde vibe—you're playing as a couple, something that makes total sense given Rockstar's appetite for telling stories with emotional stakes. As well as jumping between the two characters GTA 5-style, you can spend time roaming and robbing the world together as a couple, which strengthens your relationship. The more time you hang out together, the better their bond. Can you force them to break up if you solely play as Lucia and treat Jason like human wallpaper? No. There's no dumping your significant other, but you can expect the type of affinity you build to be reflected in the story. Additionally, being the perfect couple doesn't provide any gameplay benefits, and so there’s no need to put extra effort into the relationship if you don’t want to. It’s completely optional; they’ll be there for each other no matter if you regularly interact with the couple mechanics or ignore them completely.

"They will remain partners in crime,” Nelson confirms. “You will always have the benefit of working together and having each other's back – whether they're romantically close or not doesn't change that. They will still work together. It's really about what you want for them, their story, and how it plays out. Whether you've nurtured the relationship or not will definitely have a bearing on how their story plays out."

As well as potential variations to how the story can play out, Jason and Lucia being a couple does build into GTA 6’s gameplay systems, too. In the middle of a crime spree, you can go your separate ways to avoid police who are looking for a couple, or if one character gets into trouble with a random NPC, the other will back them up. But the relationship shows up in the little ways as well as the big. Checking in via text, holding hands, shopping, holding the door open—it all adds up.

When Nelson first loaded up his save for the demo, we were transported to a downtown part of Leonida. Our stroll around there was anything but casual. The streets, traffic, and sheer number of NPCs of all shapes and sizes - and their penchant for screaming curses at you - hit like a slap in the face. It's enough to make you feel like an Amish kid on Rumspringer in New York. You overhear chunks of pedestrian dialogue that sound like real conversations, there are stores and bodegas and pawn shops all ripe for the robbing, and it's all rendered in such detail that your eyes overload for a few seconds.

The life this world seems to have isn't just noise and style either. NPCs now have a wide range of tolerance for any BS you may or may not throw their way. Taunt them, and they could act offended or even attack you. Pull a gun, and they could cower or choose to escalate. Get into an altercation, and maybe you'll attract the attention of an entirely different group of people that want to get all up in your business.

"I think in previous GTA games you were a bit all-powerful,” says Nelson. “You were the only one with an invisible arsenal hidden away. Apart from the police, everyone would run in terror from you if you started acting out. This world in GTA 6 is not like that."

To help you navigate this new, complex ecosystem, the way you interact with the world has evolved since GTA 5. Building on the control system introduced in Red Dead Redemption 2, using L2 doesn't immediately aim your gun if it's holstered. Instead, you can use it to talk to or taunt characters you meet. According to Nelson, this small system required a huge technical effort across animators, designers, and dialogue writers. It appears as if it’s been worth the hassle, though, as it made the interactions I saw feel more organic and authentic than the comparatively stilted NPC back-and-forths you often see in other open-world games.

After an unfortunate run-in with a douchebag of a guy and some trigger-happy women who happened to be jogging past, we got confirmation that the Wanted level mechanic is still alive and well in GTA 6. If you're spotted committing a crime, police will respond and, depending on the situation, will get a description of you, your car, your clothing, and whether or not you're walking around as a couple or separately. Changing any of those things can aid your escape, as can swapping your car for an on-foot sprint through the city. After the douchebag incident, Lucia got away on one of those scooters that lie around the streets in big cities. A smart move, considering that making a getaway behind the wheel presents more issues than players have experienced before.

"The streets in this game are narrower and more realistic in terms of scale. Which, in addition to all the density of the traffic on the roads, makes driving slightly more challenging and requires a bit of skill," warns Nelson.

Oh, and not only is the driving tougher, even just stealing the car has evolved to be a more nuanced process too. It's still the automobile acquisition thrill that we know and love; it's just deeper than a simple smash and grab.

"We have put some layers of stratification into the vehicles," explains Nelson. "Previously, you could just press triangle to automatically hotwire and steal any vehicle that you wanted and take off. We felt like that left a lot of potential gameplay on the table in terms of progression and decision-making for players. So now, you start off the game and there are certain parked cars that are not accessible to you until you get a bit further along with the story and you acquire certain tools to get into them, but you can always carjack any driver you see."

“I think it gives all the vehicles more meaning, and you need to pay attention to what you’re doing a bit more,” he adds.

Now different makes and models will need different approaches; a fancy car might come equipped with an electronic lock and require a key cloner to get into. And the danger doesn’t stop once you’re inside either. An advanced GPS tracking system may be installed that forces you to drive fast, Speed style, to avoid getting caught. To help, both Jason and Lucia have a scanning app installed on their phones that will reveal if the car you’re looking at is equipped with such technology, as well as how much cash you can make selling it or the cost of registering it for yourself.

Whether you're boosting cars or murdering NPCs, Jason and Lucia have a Criminal Profile as well as a Wanted level. A new mechanic for the Grand Theft Auto series, it changes depending on your interactions in the world. Think of it as an upgraded version of Red Dead Redemption 2’s Honor system. There, Arthur Morgan could go on a killing spree and then work his way back to sainthood by greeting everyone he met; here it's more nuanced. Get into a shootout during a robbery or fire back at an aggressor? A reasonable response. Escalate a situation that you could have walked away from without violence? That's going to change your profile. Despite this new profiling system, Nelson was at pains to point out that there's no correct way to play - Grand Theft Auto is still all about committing crimes.

"There isn’t a right or wrong way to play this game, but consistent actions may have an impact in terms of how the world reacts to you and how the narrative plays out," explains Nelson.

"In this game, you are playing as criminals on the run, but the narrative is such that it makes most sense for them to do what they need to do while not drawing unnecessary attention (even though sometimes that happens)."

As Nelson played, it was not just major moments of violence that dynamically altered the profile; smaller everyday actions seemed to make a difference, too. Throwing trash in a garbage can seemed to help, and according to Nelson, feeding animals will be another option.

When you need somewhere to relax after a hard day of building your Criminal Profile, Jason and Lucia have access to a new upgraded type of safehouse, where you can grab a drink from the fridge, give yourself a new hairstyle, and just do couple shit.

"The safehouses in this game are probably closer to the camps in RDR2 than they are to safehouses in any GTA game before in terms of how interactive they are and how much they feel like your home," says Nelson.

Don't go thinking the Grand Theft Auto brand has gone too domestic bliss, though; it seems like the weird and wonderful satire you expect from Rockstar is all present and correct. NPCs still shout unhinged things about mommy issues and peeing on you for cash; there's an attorney that works out of a dumpster for pills, and there are more of those deliciously dark TV ads than ever before. Social media returns in a big way, and even if Jason and Lucia aren't posting themselves - they're a couple on the run, after all - they still get to lurk and doomscroll like the rest of us.

"That’s a question a lot of people ask: how do you deal with satire in today’s world? I think there’s always stuff to satirize. As long as humans are humans, other humans will figure out ways to satirize what we do," says Nelson. It's clearly a tough balancing act, though, and he points out that unlike a TV show that comes out every week, the targets the game chooses have to stay relevant through a long development cycle.

"We have to be careful that what we’re choosing to satirize is not going to feel dated in a weird way. I think those broader things are OK to satirize, but very specific political issues or memes will date fast. Even the way our characters speak, we think about it a lot so that they're not using extremely contemporary slang. Even though our characters are a certain age, they need to feel somewhat timeless."

So aside from a need to avoid referencing outdated memes or dusty slang, what have those 13 years since the last game – and the new technology that came with them – meant for Grand Theft Auto?

"The density of GTA 6 has been an exciting challenge, but that's also part of the reason why our team has doubled in size," says Nelson.

"One of the coolest things about this game being developed from the ground up on this generation of hardware is taking advantage of all the memory that we have on the latest generation of consoles, combined with our teams’ experience doing this for so long together."

If you had told me Rockstar had spent 13 years on the mo-cap alone, I wouldn't immediately call bullshit. It's the best I've ever seen a game look on PS5, and it could hold its own against most high-end PC games too. Everything from the facial expressions to the sway of Lucia's walk – genuinely, one of the first things I noticed about the character is the way she moves realistically for her height and build, rather than like a male character with boobs attached – to the lights on a boat traveling through the sea around Leonida, actual realistic-looking hair, and the skyline and sun glinting off cars as they race by.

It’s notable that, for its very first gameplay presentation to the press, what Rockstar chose to show wasn’t a dramatic set piece; it was a slice of the world. It was a ballsy move that showed an eagerness to signal to players just how much awaits them in this new, bigger, and better criminal playground.

"I just really wanted to show that, in addition to what we hope will be a very compelling story for people to get involved in, there is a very deep, vast, incredible world to explore and get involved with as these two characters – apart, or together, however you want to play it,” says Nelson. “And finally, even though there are some new systems at play, it's still very much Grand Theft Auto."

That bit at the end of the latest trailer, when Jason's friend Cal Hampton is talking about appreciating the present? I can't help feeling that it reflects how Rockstar wants us all to play in its new open world, exploring, getting sidetracked, discovering things for ourselves, enjoying life in this fully-realised digital city, and not just burning through the story like it's a race. That's confidence and a sign that the team sees the Leonida they've built as the crown jewel of GTA 6. The biggest takeaway? Those streets are going to be home to the best type of chaos.

Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on November 19.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: In GTA 6 You’re Not Just Wanted, You’re Hunted
articles.summary: The wanted system in GTA 6 has been totally overhauled to give the police even more tools to hunt you, as well as new methods for players to evade being busted.
articles.body:
There are dozens of mechanics, ideas, and quirks that are considered core to Grand Theft Auto’s identity. The wide variety of vehicles; a cast of oddball criminals; radio stations playing hit after hit after hit; toilet humour packed into every billboard, product brand, and TV ad. But there’s one thing arguably more foundational than all those ideas, something that the entire concept of GTA was built upon: car chases. Since the very beginning, the series’ central hook has been committing crimes and getting away with it. The “getting away” part has, more often than not, been literal – tearing through the city streets as cops do everything in their power to put you behind bars.

Those chases, inspired by cinema’s best getaways, are manifested by Grand Theft Auto’s wanted system – an escalating state of emergency that sees the city’s police force deploy fiercer and fiercer measures as the severity of your crimes increases. Originally represented by four pixelated police heads, it evolved into the trademark star system – a single star causing just a couple of beat cops to investigate a pedestrian collision or break up an unarmed assault, and racking up a full six stars summoning a battalion of militarised law enforcement with the goal of putting an end to your unstoppable murder spree. The system has changed and advanced with each new game, and that evolution does not stop with GTA 6.

After Grand Theft Auto 5 dropped the number of stars by one to both streamline the system and match the five in the title, GTA 6 sees the full six stars returned to the HUD for the first time since 2009’s Chinatown Wars. While it’s still much too early to know the nuanced criteria for triggering each of those stars, during our hands-off demo at Rockstar’s Edinburgh HQ we saw that there are several new factors involved beyond the individual wanted levels themselves.

“We have this heat system,” explains Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North. “[The police] know what I look like and what I’m wearing. [If I find] a pair of glasses – I'll put on this and this baseball hat. But they still know what I'm wearing, so I would need to go to a clothing store or call my personal vehicle, which has changes of outfits in the trunk.”

“Changing your hair will change your appearance,” he continues, “but the police will still know what you are wearing, so not great if I am standing out in the open.”

Sitting beneath the row of wanted stars on the HUD are a series of new red icons, each of which identifies the level of information the police have on you. So far, we’ve seen three:

A silhouette of a person indicates that the police have a physical description of you.

A clothes hanger denotes that the police know what clothing you are wearing.

A camera means that the police have witnessed you on CCTV security footage.

It appears the system goes even deeper than that, though. “You can see with these little icons on-screen, the police know what we're driving,” says Nelson, “so we should just jump out the vehicle. They also know we're a couple. You could split up, and that will also help lower the police’s perception of you.”

These factors add new layers to GTA’s foundational wanted system. Naturally, they influence the way the police force’s artificial intelligence is able to track you through the state of Leonida.

“The Wanted system in GTA 6 requires that someone witness the crime, or an alarm needs to be set off for it to be reported to the law,” Nelson explains. “Our dispatch is extremely specific in what it knows.”

The more information the police have, the easier it will be for them to find you. While our hands-off didn’t delve into the depths of how it all works, the possibilities are already dizzying – could Rockstar have gone as far as to create a system where cops can build a profile of you via Snapmatic and Lifeinvader photos posted by Vice City’s social media-obsessed public? GTA 5’s pedestrians were able to call 911 from their phones to report crimes that went unwitnessed by law enforcement, so it seems realistic to believe that the wider population will impact the wanted system in additional ways this time around.

Regardless of how deep the individual mechanics go, it’s clear that Rockstar intends to ratchet up the tension of each and every getaway. You’re not just wanted by the cops, but actively hunted by a force that can utilize multiple information sources and data points to narrow their search. It’s a natural evolution of Red Dead Redemption 2’s bounty system brought into the modern world — and the similarities don’t stop there. As in Red Dead, you become wanted in specific regions of the world, and returning to that area will see you face the consequences.

“I can check my map – this is a hot area,” says Nelson. “The cops are there. If I go back, they'll be hanging around for a little while. If I hover back over that area of the map, I [can see I] still have one star in that area.”

“We could wait for it to die down, change our outfits, or split Jason and Lucia up. There’s a lot of smart things we could do.”

The most fascinating aspect of this system is not the apparent enhancements to police AI routines, though, but the promise of new gameplay opportunities. GTA’s police have long been able to recognise your vehicle, and a quick stop-off at the local Pay ‘n’ Spray was a fast-pass to douse the heat. But now that applies to our human protagonists – in our demo we watched as Jason purchased a baseball cap from a convenience store, which when worn removed the “description” icon from the HUD. But it didn’t remove the “clothing” icon, which indicates the system’s depth – Jason was still wearing the same clothes and could still be identified by them, but the addition of the hat meant the cops’ physical description of him was now out of date. If only gifting Arthur Morgan mutton chops granted him the same peace of mind.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

It’s exciting to consider all the possibilities we will have to bamboozle the cops: stopping by the salon after a bank robbery to turn a gorgeous hairstyle into a buzz cut. Pre-packing a complete change of clothes in your getaway vehicle. Getting a full-body tattoo after an assassination. Okay, maybe that last one is a bit much, but you get the idea. In GTA 6, reducing your wanted level is about far more than evading the cops – you can actively put them off your scent.

The other thing to think about is that these new layers mean how you commit a crime is just as important as the crime itself. If being seen, either by people or CCTV cameras, arms your hunters with information, then denying them those descriptions potentially lends you a significant advantage. This makes stealth a valuable weapon – during the demo we saw Jason crouch to keep out of a police officer’s line of sight, and so we can reasonably assume that we’ll also be able to avoid the gaze of security guards, civilians, and cameras. Tactically eliminating CCTV networks or patrolling wardens before they can call in reports feel like scenarios that GTA’s new wanted system could encourage, especially considering there’s a new type of wanted level that would fit into this scenario. A “hollow” wanted star is displayed when the police are responding to a crime but have no information who the perpetrator is. Denying the flow of incriminating data to ensure you only trigger hollow wanted stars is an idea to build an entire gameplay approach around – I’m excited to see just how deep it all goes.

For the more aggressive players out there, we’ve also seen that the mask system is back, and it’ll presumably build upon the rules established in Red Dead Redemption 2 – cover your face, protect your identity, give the cops a bad day at the office. While a quieter, more tactical approach could perhaps allow you to slip in and out without raising the alarm, this is still GTA, and so there’s going to be some mayhem. A mask – be it a securely-tied bandana or a rubbery famous face – will at least limit the details your victims can report to your hunters.

But even in moments of direct confrontation, there are ways to ensure the subsequent manhunt goes in your favour. ”There is more nuance to how you can get away with things,” says Nelson. A good example of this is the way NPCs respond to threats – in our demo we watched as Jason aimed a gun at a group of aggressors, but held short of pulling the trigger. Rather than just default to engaging in violence, the enemies thought better of it and fled the scene. While the crime was reported and the police were on their way, they weren't responding to a violent crime, and so the wanted level stayed low.

“I aimed the gun at the person, which defused the situation and they all ran,” Nelson explains. “If you commit a crime and run, get into trouble and move on before the cops get there, and you don’t start shooting people, don't start escalating, you’re generally going to be fine.”

The changes made to the wanted system tie into the larger picture of Rockstar’s intent for Grand Theft Auto 6 – this is the GTA you know and love, but each part of it has additional layers that allow you to drill deeper than you ever have before. We already know that the series’ core formula, established way back in its first 3D open world, has stood the test of time not just because it's a bulletproof idea, but because each new game has carefully reinforced it. By enhancing the wanted system, as well as interlinked mechanics like car jacking, Rockstar is making sure that in GTA 6, the things you’ve done a million times before have the potential to feel brand new.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Playthroughs Can Last 80 Hours
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 will take a while for players to finish, with the game's producer stating it took him 80 hours.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 will take a while for players to finish, with the game's producer stating it took him 80 hours.

In an The New York Times interview, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game in February. He noted that included the main story and some "optional goals with narrative ramifications," it's unclear if that included just mucking about in the open world or anything, though. Still, that is a sizable length regardless. Nelson ultimately hopes fans take their time with the game and don't rush through it.

For comparison, GTA 4 and 5 are around 30 hours long, while Red Dead Redemption 2 is around 50-60 hours. So, that means GTA 6 will be the longest of Rockstar's games to date, which will be reassuring for fans who have waited a long time for this game. Assuming 80 hours doesn't include the time for 100% completion, there will still be plenty of ways to extend your time with the game.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

Grand Theft Auto 6 has no shortage of open-world activities, including basketball, fishing, exercising, and much more. There will also likely be a plethora of side missions for players to indulge in, so it seems like we'll all be playing GTA 6 for a long time. Red Dead Redemption 2 has kept players very active thanks to its level of depth and detail, thanks to unique NPCs, hidden details, and side content.

In case your appetite for GTA 6 content hasn't been satiated yet, IGN has no shortage of GTA 6 coverage. That includes an exclusive preview of the game , our own interview with Rob Nelson , and all kinds of breakdowns regarding new gameplay details , songs , and more.
